program: Sound Design for Audiovisual Media (Sound / Ton)
university: Filmuniversität Babelsberg KONRAD WOLF
institutionType: Public film school (film university)
durationEcts: Programme page states 6 semesters / 120 LP (ECTS). The 6-semester figure is unusual for a 120-LP master — confirm with the programme office.
language: German (DSH-1 German certificate is a hard admission condition)
focus: Film/Game Sound; Sound Design; Recording/Engineering; Immersive Audio
whatYouStudy: Four core domains: audio engineering, sound mixing, acoustics/signal processing, and music. Students plan and deliver cinema sound mixes and act as sound supervisors on real film productions, building an individual 'sound language' through interdisciplinary artistic projects. Heavy Pro Tools use (the entrance exam itself is a Pro Tools scoring task). Strong industry pipeline into Babelsberg Studios.
entryRequirements: Completed B.F.A. in Sound, a Tonmeister degree, or a comparable subject-specific degree; uni-assist evaluation for foreign qualifications; German at DSH-1 minimum; medical certificate of normal hearing plus an audiogram, both issued within the last year.
acceptsNonMusic: No. The page requires a "completed Bachelor of Fine Arts in Sound, Tonmeister, or comparable subject-specific degree". A software-engineering BSc is not a comparable subject-specific degree, and no alternative talent route is offered.
portfolioSpec: Documentation of works from the past three years, max 12 pages (PDF). Video compilation of at least THREE films on which the applicant did the sound design, 15 minutes total (MPG/MPEG/MP4/MOV/WMV, max 3.5 GB). At least ONE piece of music recorded or mixed by the applicant (WAV/MP3/MP4, max 5 GB). Tabular CV describing musical development.
auditionSpec: On-site three-part aptitude test: (1) music test — intervals, harmonies, piano audition, critical listening/audio evaluation; (2) interview — presentation of submitted work plus subject knowledge; (3) practical exam — scoring a scene in Pro Tools.
applicationOpens: 12 April (per the programme's own application page)
deadline: 18 May 2027 for the winter-semester 2027/28 intake, as published on the application page. Verify directly — the page may still be showing an earlier cycle.
tuitionIntl: No tuition (Brandenburg public institution). Only a semester contribution/administrative fee; exact amount UNVERIFIED.
scholarship: DAAD Study Scholarships – Master Studies (open to Tunisian graduates; funding usually starts 1 October); Deutschlandstipendium
stipend: DAAD graduate scholarship pays a monthly stipend plus travel allowance and health insurance; exact 2027 monthly rate UNVERIFIED. The university itself pays nothing.
facilities: Germany's oldest film school (founded 1954) on the historic Babelsberg Studios site, 30 min from Berlin. Cinema mixing stages, Dolby-standard theatrical mixing, full film-sound post chain. Reported acceptance rate 3–5% (secondary source, UNVERIFIED).
fitNotes: Best-in-class for film sound in Europe, but effectively closed to him: it demands a prior sound/Tonmeister degree, DSH-1 German, an audiogram, and a portfolio of three finished films he has already mixed. Also the wrong target anyway — it trains film sound supervisors, not DJs/producers.

program: Musikregie (Tonmeister) – Master of Music
university: Hochschule für Musik Detmold – Erich-Thienhaus-Institut (ETI)
institutionType: Public conservatory / Musikhochschule
durationEcts: UNVERIFIED (one aggregator lists 1 year; the ETI pages do not state duration or ECTS)
focus: Recording/Engineering; Music Production (classical/acoustic recording direction)
whatYouStudy: Artistic recording direction (Musikregie): responsibility for the artistic result and quality of a music production. Combines musical-communicative competence with technical foundations and extensive hands-on practice in the ETI recording studios; work in broadcasting, film and TV, opera houses and theatres. Sister programme Musikübertragung (B.Mus.) is the bachelor-level Tonmeister track; a Music Acoustics M.Sc./Dr.-Ing. also sits at the ETI.
entryRequirements: Bachelor's degree in Music Recording (Musikübertragung) or a Tonmeister diploma; proof of German; proof of health insurance; successful aptitude test.
acceptsNonMusic: No. The requirement is explicitly a "Bachelor's degree in Music Recording respectively diploma in Tonmeister". A music-specific/Tonmeister degree is required; no talent-based exception is published.
portfolioSpec: Tabular CV; written statement explaining the choice of programme and intended study focus; a CD/DVD containing THREE productions made by the applicant within the past year.
auditionSpec: Aptitude test: presentation of the three submitted productions plus a colloquium of approx. 30 minutes covering musical repertoire, technical principles and studio experience. Assessed by at least two committee members as 'qualified' / 'not qualified'.
applicationOpens: 1 October (summer semester) / 15 February (winter semester)
deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date: winter semester 15 February–15 March; summer semester 1 October–1 November (as published, no year stated).
tuitionIntl: No tuition (NRW public). Semester fee only; exact amount UNVERIFIED.
scholarship: DAAD Study Scholarships – Master Studies for Artists/All Disciplines; Deutschlandstipendium
facilities: The Erich-Thienhaus-Institut is the internationally leading German Tonmeister school; multiple recording studios and control rooms, strong links to broadcasters, opera houses and labels. Detailed console/immersive-room specs are in a scanned brochure that could not be reliably read — UNVERIFIED.
fitNotes: The gold standard for classical recording engineering in Germany, and completely out of reach for him: it requires a Tonmeister bachelor plus three of his own studio productions from the last 12 months, in German. Also classical-recording-oriented, not electronic/club music. List it as a long-term aspiration, not a 2027 application.

program: Popular Music M.A. – specialisation Producing / Composing Artist
university: Popakademie Baden-Württemberg
institutionType: Public university of popular music (state Hochschule)
durationEcts: 4 semesters / 120 ECTS, full-time
language: German (B2 required of international applicants by the end of the first semester)
focus: Music Production; Electronic Music Production
whatYouStudy: Two-stage structure: year 1 taught courses, year 2 an independent master project. The Producing/Composing track covers songwriting, arrangement, recording, sound design, beat programming, mixing, mastering, electronic music production, film music, game music, vocal producing and music-business practice — plus working as a production service provider for band projects. Facilities include professional recording studios (Tonstudio), the SMIX.LAB and a media library. Germany's only state Hochschule dedicated to popular music.
entryRequirements: Completed first degree with a standard duration of at least 6 semesters; advanced practical musical experience; department-specific entrance examination; German B2 for international applicants by the end of the first semester.
acceptsNonMusic: Check. The published requirement is only "a completed undergraduate degree with a minimum standard study duration of 6 semesters" — no subject restriction is stated, so his BSc Software Engineering satisfies the formal condition. Admission is decided almost entirely by the practical entrance exam, which does demand advanced musical ability.
portfolioSpec: Upload of own musical productions; for performing/educating artists at least one live video (max 200 MB). Additional accepted material: videos, press coverage, photographs, cover artwork, scores, lyrics, teaching concepts. Exact number of tracks required for Producing/Composing is not specified on the application page — UNVERIFIED.
auditionSpec: Live entrance examination (Aufnahmeprüfung), format varies by department. Typically 2–3 pieces performed, often the applicant's own compositions, with up to three accompanying musicians or playback; plus theory examination, improvisation test and interview.
applicationOpens: UNVERIFIED (portal typically opens in the winter preceding the deadline)
deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date: 30 April (23:59 UTC upload deadline) for the following winter semester.
tuitionIntl: No tuition for a first degree at the Popakademie itself, BUT Baden-Württemberg's LHGebG charges non-EU/EEA international students €1,500 per semester (≈€6,000 over 4 semesters). As a Tunisian national he falls under this fee.
scholarship: DAAD Study Scholarships – Master Studies (Tunisia eligible); Deutschlandstipendium. No Popakademie-specific scholarship found.
facilities: Professional recording studios, SMIX.LAB, mediathek; faculty of working industry producers; located in Mannheim's Musikpark start-up cluster with dense German music-industry links.
fitNotes: The single closest match in Germany to "I want to be a producer": actual beat programming, electronic production, mixing and mastering, taught by industry practitioners. Two obstacles: German B2 and a genuinely demanding live entrance exam, plus €1,500/semester as a non-EU student. He should treat this as his main German target and spend 2026–27 building a producer audition set and German.

program: Filmton / Sounddesign (Diplomaufbaustudium – postgraduate diploma at master level)
university: Filmakademie Baden-Württemberg
institutionType: Public film school (state-owned GmbH)
durationEcts: 4 semesters plus 1 diploma semester (5 semesters total); ECTS not published — UNVERIFIED
focus: Film/Game Sound; Sound Design; Immersive Audio
whatYouStudy: Year 1 concentrates on production/location sound; year 2 on post-production. Covers original sound recording on set, sound design, dialogue editing, mixing technique, working with Foley artists, film-music recording and Dolby Atmos. Optional specialisations in media design and sound for games. Entirely project-based — students score the academy's own film productions.
entryRequirements: Postgraduate (Aufbaustudium) structure implies a completed prior degree; Hochschulreife plus, where held, officially certified Vordiplom/Diplom/Bachelor/Master must be submitted. No music degree is demanded.
acceptsNonMusic: Check — most likely yes. It is a Diplomaufbaustudium with no stated subject restriction and no explicit prohibition on non-music backgrounds; the filter is the practical entrance exam, not the bachelor subject. Confirm in writing before applying.
portfolioSpec: Own projects/work samples uploaded via the online portal. Video work samples: max 1 GB, MP4 container, H.264 codec, data rate 15 MB/s. Exact number and duration of required audio samples not published — UNVERIFIED.
auditionSpec: Pre-selection on the file, then an on-site entrance examination (Aufnahmeprüfung) conducted in Pro Tools. Applicants must bring working knowledge of recording, sound design, mixing and bouncing.
applicationOpens: UNVERIFIED (online portal typically opens in the autumn)
deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date: 15 February.
tuitionIntl: €0 for EU citizens; €1,500 for non-EU citizens per the programme page (whether this is per semester under the BW LHGebG or a one-off is not clarified on the page — confirm).
scholarship: DAAD Study Scholarships (Film/Fine Art strand); Deutschlandstipendium. No academy-specific scholarship found.
facilities: State-of-the-art audio post-production studios and current-industry on-set equipment, Dolby Atmos mixing, Foley stage; part of one of Europe's most production-active film schools with heavy German TV/film industry placement.
fitNotes: The most realistic German film-sound route for someone without a music degree — the gate is a Pro Tools practical test rather than a conservatory audition, and the fee is low. But it makes film/game sound designers, not DJs. Worth applying only if he genuinely wants a screen-audio career alongside producing.

program: Zeitabhängige Medien / Sound – Vision (sub-programme of Sound–Vision–Games)
university: HAW Hamburg – Hochschule für Angewandte Wissenschaften, Dept. Medientechnik
institutionType: University of applied sciences (public)
durationEcts: 3 semesters (90 ECTS per aggregator; the HAW page states 3 semesters, ECTS UNVERIFIED on the official page)
language: German (C1 required); English B1 also tested at interview
focus: Sound Design; Immersive Audio; Recording/Engineering; Live/Event audio
whatYouStudy: Project-centred study at the intersection of science, technology and creative design. Modules cover audio technology and sound design, video technology and image design, VFX production, interactive design, lighting technology and design, plus production and project management. Eight required/elective modules in the chosen branch. Graduates go into audio/video/lighting manufacturers, production studios and theatres. Nationally unique in linking sound, moving image and games.
entryRequirements: Bachelor's degree with at least 210 ECTS in media technology, media systems, computer science, IT (applied IT or media specialism welcome), communication design, illustration or a related subject; German C1; English B1; passed aptitude test.
acceptsNonMusic: Yes — explicitly. The accepted-degree list names "computer science, IT (applicants with a degree in applied IT or with a specialism in media are welcome)". Caveat: it requires 210 ECTS, and many 3-year BSc degrees are 180 ECTS — he must check his SMU MedTech credit total.
portfolioSpec: Between 3 and 10 work samples that "demonstrate your interest in and your aptitude and potential for your chosen branch" in detail and comprehensively. Accepted types: video, animation, light design, light installation, sound design, soundscape, music production, installation, performance, interactive/multimedia work.
auditionSpec: Two-stage aptitude assessment: (1) portfolio/work-sample review; (2) interview if stage 1 is passed, at which German C1 and English B1 are verified. No instrumental audition.
applicationOpens: 1 October (registration for the aptitude test)
deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date: aptitude-test registration 1–31 October (one source says 'until 14 October'); formal application for the study place 1 December–15 January; entry SUMMER semester only, starting early April.
tuitionIntl: No tuition. Semester contribution €397, including the semester ticket and the Germany-wide rail pass (Deutschlandticket).
scholarship: DAAD Study Scholarships – Master Studies for All Academic Disciplines; Deutschlandstipendium
facilities: Art and Media Campus Finkenau, Hamburg: audio, video and lighting labs, studios for sound design and interactive media. Facility detail beyond the campus address is UNVERIFIED.
fitNotes: Structurally the friendliest German public option for a software-engineering graduate — CS degrees are named as welcome, the gate is a portfolio not an audition, and the total cost is €397 a semester. Two catches: German C1 (high), and the intake is April only, so a September 2027 start is impossible — he would target April 2027 (apply Oct 2026–Jan 2027) or April 2028. It is also more media/event technology than club-music production.

program: Integrative Komposition (M.Mus.) – specialisation Elektronische Komposition (ICEM)
university: Folkwang Universität der Künste
institutionType: Public art university (music, theatre, dance, design)
durationEcts: 4 semesters full-time (part-time possible) / 120 ECTS
focus: Electronic Music / Live Electronics; Electroacoustic Composition; Sonic Arts
whatYouStudy: Project-oriented master built around the student's own artistic development project. Four combinable specialisations: Electronic Composition, Instrumental Composition, Pop Composition, and Composition & Visualisation — students may mix them with different weightings. Teaching happens in the ICEM (Institut für Computermusik und Elektronische Medien), which has trained electroacoustic composers since 1971 and shaped the current Integrative Komposition degrees.
entryRequirements: A first university degree on which the master builds, OR proof of outstanding artistic talent; artistic aptitude established through the Eignungsprüfung; German B1 at enrolment; €50 application fee.
acceptsNonMusic: Yes, in practice. The page states applicants need "a first university degree which the Master study course is based on" and separately allows entry on "proof of outstanding artistic talent"; the programme welcomes non-music backgrounds provided artistic aptitude is proven. The portfolio, not the degree subject, decides.
portfolioSpec: Stage-1 digital submission of own works "in the form of original scores (especially for instrumental composition), recordings, videos etc." PLUS a concept/project plan for an artistic development project describing the intended master-thesis topic. Formats PDF and MP4, max 100 MB total. No fixed number of works is stated.
auditionSpec: Two-stage Eignungsprüfung. Stage 1: digital preliminary round — portfolio and master-project draft assessed for technical/artistic ability and feasibility. Stage 2: in-person main round — approx. 30-minute colloquium on the submitted works, any revisions, artistic development and engagement with current artistic trends.
applicationOpens: UNVERIFIED
deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date: 15 March for the following winter semester; 15 November for the following summer semester.
tuitionIntl: No tuition (NRW). €50 application fee plus the semester social contribution (Studierendenwerk + NRW semester ticket); amount UNVERIFIED.
scholarship: DAAD Study Scholarships – Master Studies for Artists (Music strand), Tunisia eligible; Deutschlandstipendium
facilities: ICEM — one of Germany's oldest and most respected computer-music/electronic-media institutes (studio for live-electronic music since 1971), with a historic technical instrument collection; regular PACT Zollverein collaborations.
fitNotes: A genuinely open door: no music degree strictly required, the decision rests on a portfolio plus a project concept, and it is tuition-free. But this is art-music electronic composition (electroacoustic, live electronics, installation), not dance-floor production — he would need to frame his work as compositional practice, and reach German B1.

program: Elektronische Komposition – Master of Music
university: Hochschule für Musik und Tanz Köln (HfMT Köln)
institutionType: Public conservatory (Europe's largest music academy)
durationEcts: 4 semesters / 120 ECTS
focus: Electronic Music / Live Electronics; Electroacoustic Composition
whatYouStudy: Independent compositional work and professionalisation: mixed instrumental/electronic composition, installations and internet works, plus self-organised concerts of student-created music. The electronic and instrumental composition classes work closely together, so students can join the other class's projects and take main-subject lessons there. All practical work takes place in the Studio für Elektronische Musik.
entryRequirements: "Successful completion of a four-year bachelor's degree in composition or equivalent"; an undergraduate degree in instrumental composition also qualifies; good computer skills (no prior electronics study needed); German A2 minimum; application via muvac.
acceptsNonMusic: Essentially No. The page states that "Bachelor graduates from other art or computer science fields" are admitted only "in exceptional cases of exceptional talent". Computer science is named — but as an exception route requiring exceptional demonstrated talent, not a normal pathway.
portfolioSpec: Own works must be submitted for evaluation and are presented and discussed at the colloquium. The specific number, duration and format of works is not stated on the programme page — UNVERIFIED (submission runs through the muvac platform).
auditionSpec: Qualifying examination consisting of a colloquium: presentation and discussion of the submitted works, with questions on the applicant's own musical aesthetics and prior knowledge of contemporary music. No instrumental audition mentioned.
applicationOpens: UNVERIFIED
deadline: UNVERIFIED — no deadline published on the programme page; applications run through muvac. Confirm with the Studio für Elektronische Musik.
tuitionIntl: No tuition (NRW). Semester social contribution only; amount UNVERIFIED.
scholarship: DAAD Study Scholarships – Master Studies for Artists (Music); Deutschlandstipendium
facilities: Studio für Elektronische Musik with several fixed and mobile workstations, comprehensive software/hardware and "excellent listening facilities"; Cologne is the historic home of the legendary WDR Studio for Electronic Music (Stockhausen).
fitNotes: Prestigious and free, and the German bar is unusually low (A2). But the entry wording is the problem: without a composition bachelor he lands in the "exceptional talent" exception, which is a very high evidentiary bar for someone with no prior music training. Also purely art-music, no production/DJ content.

program: Multimedia Composition (Multimediale Komposition) – Master
university: Hochschule für Musik und Theater Hamburg (HfMT Hamburg)
institutionType: Public conservatory / Musikhochschule
durationEcts: 2 years (4 semesters) / 120 ECTS
language: English (the entrance examination is conducted in English). German B2 reported as required of international applicants by a secondary source — confirm with the Hochschule.
focus: Electronic Music / Live Electronics; Sonic Arts; Immersive/Interactive Audio
whatYouStudy: Interdisciplinary programme for composers, media artists and computer scientists with musical interests. Fields: algorithmic composition, live electronics, game-engine development, video and light programming, digital recording, interactive installations, microtonal composition. Software explicitly taught: Max/MSP/Jitter, Ableton Live, Unreal Engine, MadMapper, TouchDesigner, Lightkey. Access to an AV Media Center and a digital recording studio.
entryRequirements: Completed bachelor's degree in music, composition, media art OR computer science; submission of artistic works; passed entrance examination. Language requirement: examination in English; German B2 reported for international applicants (secondary source).
acceptsNonMusic: Yes — best fit in Germany on this criterion. The programme is described as "aimed at applicants with a completed Bachelor's degree in music, composition, media art, or computer science" and is "designed for composers, media artists, and computer scientists with musical interests". A software-engineering BSc is squarely within scope.
portfolioSpec: "At least three representative works which demonstrate the ability to artistically incorporate the use of digital media, especially in the field of computer music. These works can be in the form of scores, texts, recordings, computer programs, videos, etc. and/or interactive websites."
auditionSpec: Two-part entrance examination: (1) a 3-hour written exam — interactive computer-music tasks, text analysis, and multiple-choice questions on digital-media terminology; (2) a 15-minute interview about the submitted work and the applicant's motivation. No instrumental audition.
applicationOpens: UNVERIFIED
deadline: UNVERIFIED — the programme page gives no deadline; applications are made online via the HfMT portal for the winter semester. Contact the department office.
tuitionIntl: No tuition (Hamburg public). Semester contribution only; amount UNVERIFIED.
scholarship: DAAD Study Scholarships – Master Studies (Music / All Disciplines), Tunisia eligible; Deutschlandstipendium
facilities: AV Media Center and digital recording studio; Hamburg's Musikhochschule sits in a city with a very strong electronic/club scene. Studio detail beyond this is UNVERIFIED.
fitNotes: The strongest realistic German target for him alongside the Popakademie: a CS bachelor is explicitly welcome, the portfolio can include code and interactive work as well as tracks, the entrance test rewards technical ability over conservatory ear-training, and instruction is in English. Caveat: it is computer music / installation / live electronics, not commercial dance production — he must be genuinely interested in Max/MSP and algorithmic work, and should confirm the German requirement.

program: Künstlerische Musikproduktion (Artistic Music Production) – Master of Music
university: Robert Schumann Hochschule Düsseldorf – Institut für Musik und Medien (IMM)
institutionType: Public conservatory / Musikhochschule
durationEcts: 4 semesters (2 years); ECTS not stated on the page — UNVERIFIED
focus: Music Production; Recording/Engineering
whatYouStudy: Two majors: Classical Acoustic Music Production, and Jazz and Pop Music Production. Three interwoven strands: (1) practical production work across genres and formats, exploring and applying the most recent production methods; (2) instrumental/vocal tuition with ensemble performance; (3) technical methodology and musical analysis, including acoustics and ear training. Aim is artistically independent, methodically grounded professional production work.
entryRequirements: Bachelor's degree; German B2 certificate or equivalent; successful completion of the concentration-specific proficiency test (Eignungsprüfung); €50 test fee.
acceptsNonMusic: Check — formally plausible, practically hard. The page requires a bachelor's degree without naming a subject, so a non-music degree is not excluded on paper. However the proficiency test includes an instrumental/vocal audition and written tests of musical and technical hearing, which presuppose real conservatory-level musicianship.
portfolioSpec: Work samples submitted in advance and evaluated by the committee. The exact number, length and format of the required work samples is not published on the programme page — UNVERIFIED (check the Eignungsprüfungsordnung / Anforderungen page).
auditionSpec: "The proficiency test involves the evaluation of work samples to be submitted in advance as well as completion of an instrumental/vocal audition. In addition, there is a practical task in the intended major as well as written examinations of musical and technical hearing ability." Test fee €50.
applicationOpens: UNVERIFIED
deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date: 1 March (date-of-receipt stamp of the university applies). Entry possible in winter or summer semester.
tuitionIntl: No tuition (NRW). Semester contribution and €50 proficiency-test fee; contribution amount UNVERIFIED.
scholarship: DAAD Study Scholarships – Master Studies for Artists (Music); Deutschlandstipendium
facilities: Institut für Musik und Medien (IMM) studios; RSH also runs the Ton und Bild engineering degree jointly with HS Düsseldorf, so the audio/video infrastructure is substantial. Console/immersive-room detail UNVERIFIED.
fitNotes: Content-wise excellent — a real music-production master with a Jazz/Pop track. The killer is the entrance exam: an instrumental or vocal audition plus written musical and technical ear tests. Without conservatory training he would very likely fail this, and it is in German at B2. Realistic only after two-plus years of serious instrument and ear-training work.

program: Klang und Realität (Sound and Reality) – Master of Music
university: Robert Schumann Hochschule Düsseldorf – Institut für Musik und Medien (IMM)
institutionType: Public conservatory / Musikhochschule
durationEcts: 4 semesters / 120 ECTS, full-time
focus: Sonic Arts (practice-based); Electronic Music / Live Electronics
whatYouStudy: Project-driven master integrating performative, compositional and algorithmic forms of contemporary art. Own projects sit at the centre and are re-conceptualised across two years on the basis of critical, multi-perspectival peer feedback. Two focus areas: Epistemic Media (art as a method of enquiry — acoustic research, documentary film, algorithmic composition) and Transmedia Forms (performance, sound art, installation, digital media). Musical practice is explicitly not tied to instruments.
entryRequirements: Bachelor's degree or equivalent; German B2; aptitude assessment based on a detailed project proposal. No numerus clausus.
acceptsNonMusic: Yes — explicitly. "Musical practice is not bound to musical instruments; it encompasses many approaches to art and research. Accordingly, the master's program is open to students from all disciplinary backgrounds." This is the clearest published welcome to a non-music graduate of any German programme found.
portfolioSpec: A detailed project proposal demonstrating the applicant's interests, motivations and skills, submitted with the portfolio. Number/length of accompanying works not specified — UNVERIFIED.
auditionSpec: Portfolio- and proposal-based aptitude assessment (Eignungsprüfung). No traditional instrumental entrance exam is mentioned.
applicationOpens: UNVERIFIED
deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date: 31 October, once a year. SUMMER semester entry only — courses begin at the start of April.
tuitionIntl: No tuition (NRW). Semester contribution plus €50 proficiency-test fee; contribution amount UNVERIFIED.
scholarship: DAAD Study Scholarships – Master Studies; Deutschlandstipendium
facilities: Institut für Musik und Medien studios and collaborative project spaces; detail UNVERIFIED.
fitNotes: Formally the easiest German conservatory master for him to enter — open to all disciplinary backgrounds, assessed on a project proposal, no audition, no tuition. But it is artistic-research and transmedia work, not production craft: he would leave with a conceptual sound-art practice, not DJ/producer chops. Also April-only intake, so September 2027 is not possible (target April 2027 or April 2028).

program: Audio Experience Design (Teilzeit-Master)
university: Staatliche Hochschule für Musik Trossingen
institutionType: Public conservatory / Musikhochschule
durationEcts: 4 semesters part-time at 50% workload / 60 ECTS total (15 ECTS per semester)
focus: Sound Design; Immersive Audio; Music Production (design-research framing)
whatYouStudy: "Development of audio experiences at the intersections of music, sound, language, technology, design, user experience and design research." Students pursue an individual project across the whole degree, supported by design-research seminars, interdisciplinary collaborations and guest-expert workshops. Trossingen also launched a Music Design master profile focused on Artificial Intelligence in Music (from 2023).
entryRequirements: Open to applicants from many fields and disciplines ("aus vielen Bereichen und Disziplinen"); no specific bachelor subject mandated. Motivation letter describing musical/design background plus evidence of publications or competition results.
acceptsNonMusic: Yes. The page states the programme welcomes entrants "aus vielen Bereichen und Disziplinen" and mandates no specific bachelor's degree — a software-engineering background is compatible, and a design/UX-audio framing plays to his CS strengths.
portfolioSpec: Project concept comprising: a self-introduction video of max 2 minutes; a written description of max 3 pages; and up to SEVEN previous works with accompanying descriptions.
auditionSpec: No on-site aptitude test — "Es gibt keine Aufnahmeprüfung in Präsenz." Selection includes a short video interview of approximately 15 minutes.
applicationOpens: 1 March
deadline: 1 March – 1 April, for the winter-semester intake (page references a start in October 2026 — for an October 2027 start, confirm the new window).
tuitionIntl: "Keine Studiengebühren für EU-Bürger:innen bei Erstmaster" (no tuition for EU citizens on a first master). As a non-EU national he falls under Baden-Württemberg's €1,500/semester LHGebG fee unless a part-time exemption applies — UNVERIFIED, confirm directly.
scholarship: DAAD Study Scholarships – Master Studies; Deutschlandstipendium. Note: DAAD scholarships generally require full-time enrolment, which a 50% part-time master may not satisfy — check before relying on this.
facilities: UNVERIFIED — no studio/console detail published on the programme page.
fitNotes: Uniquely low-friction entry: no in-person audition, a video interview, and up to seven free-form works as portfolio — ideal for someone with a self-taught catalogue. But it is 50% part-time and only 60 ECTS, sits in a very small town, is taught in German, and is oriented to audio UX/design research rather than club music. Also a part-time degree complicates both DAAD funding and a German student visa.

program: Creative Production (Music) MA
university: Catalyst — Institute for Creative Arts and Technology, Berlin
degree: MA validated by Plymouth Marjon University (UK). A UK-validated master's delivered in Germany — confirm German recognition (anabin/KMK) if he ever needs the degree recognised in the German public system.
institutionType: Private art/technology institute (formerly dBs Berlin / BIMM Berlin lineage), UK-validated
focus: Music Production; Electronic Music/Live Electronics; Sonic Arts (practice-based); Immersive/Spatial Audio
durationEcts: 1 year full-time or 2 years part-time. ECTS not stated on the page — UNVERIFIED.
tuitionIntl: Full-time: €6,028 per semester × 2 semesters, or €11,693 for the year paid annually (3% discount). Part-time: €3,678 per semester × 4, or €7,134/year annually. Plus a non-refundable enrolment fee of €895 per year. No EU/non-EU fee distinction is stated — non-EU students pay the same as EU students, which is unusual and favourable. A €1,000 tuition discount is offered for priority-deadline applications, and a €500 discount for students who did a Catalyst Summer Course within two years.
scholarship: No Catalyst-funded scholarship open to non-EU students was found. BAföG eligibility and national funding schemes are mentioned but those are for German/EU-resident students. "None found" for a Tunisian national — however the fee itself is low by private-academy standards.
fundingLevel: None found (but low-fee: c. €12,600/yr all-in including enrolment fee)
entryRequirements: Bachelor's degree with honours (e.g. UK 2:1) in a relevant discipline; non-standard entry considered on professional/life experience. English: IELTS 6 equivalent (B2 for applicants from Germany/EU countries). Application materials required: personal and educational information, education documentation, a "Detailed project proposal", a sample of research/academic writing, and a portfolio.
acceptsNonMusic: Check — the page says "relevant discipline" and separately allows non-standard entry on professional or life experience, but it does NOT explicitly address non-music bachelors. UNVERIFIED as to whether a software-engineering BSc counts as relevant. Given the programme is practice-as-research and portfolio-driven, the portfolio and project proposal will carry the decision. Ask admissions directly.
portfolioSpec: Required submissions listed: a "Detailed project proposal", a "sample of research/academic writing", and a "portfolio". The number of works, durations and file formats are NOT specified on the page — UNVERIFIED. Note the academic-writing sample: this is a research-led MA and it expects you to write, not only produce.
auditionSpec: No audition or on-site test mentioned on the page. Interview not mentioned — UNVERIFIED.
applicationOpens: UNVERIFIED. Given the 30 April visa-applicant deadline, applications plainly open well before that — expect autumn 2026 for the September 2027 intake.
deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. As published for the 2026 intake: visa-required applicants 30 April 2026; EU/visa-exempt 5 June 2026; late applications 28 August 2026 subject to availability. For September 2027 expect an equivalent late-April 2027 deadline for visa applicants — as a Tunisian national he falls in the EARLIEST bracket, roughly ten months before the course starts. A priority-deadline application earns a €1,000 tuition discount.
facilities: Located in the Funkhaus Berlin — the former GDR state radio complex, one of the most significant recording buildings in Europe. "Access to industry-standard facilities and tons of bookable gear" including studios, the MONOM 4D multichannel spatial-audio composition system, and modular synthesis equipment. Berlin itself is the global centre of gravity for electronic music.
whatYouStudy: Five practice-as-research modules: Imagine (research proposal), Contextualise (field review), Investigate, Present (public-facing work), Synthesise (final body of work), with concurrent workshops in Creative Sound Practices and Contexts of Listening, plus one-to-one and group supervision. You define your own artistic project and the school supervises it — "reshape your music practice and pursue your chosen area of interest, desired specialisation or passion project through practice-based artistic research".
fitNotes: Strategically the best value in this slice: roughly €12,600 for a full year in the Funkhaus in Berlin, in English, with no non-EU fee premium, spatial audio (MONOM 4D) and modular synthesis on site, in the world's leading city for electronic music and club culture — directly relevant to a DJ/producer ambition. Two cautions: it is a self-directed practice-as-research MA, so it assumes you already have a practice and can write about it (an academic writing sample is required), and it will not teach mixing from zero. The visa-applicant deadline of ~30 April is nearly a year ahead of enrolment — this is the one on the list he must start earliest.

program: Audio Communication and Sonology (double degree with the Institute of Sonology, Royal Conservatoire The Hague)
university: Technische Universität Berlin – Fachgebiet Audiokommunikation
institutionType: Public technical university + partner conservatory
degree: Double degree: M.Sc. (TU Berlin) + M.Mus. (Royal Conservatoire The Hague)
durationEcts: 4 semesters / 120 ECTS (60 per year); year 1 in Berlin, year 2 in The Hague
language: English plus German — English at IELTS 6.0 / TOEFL iBT 83 minimum, and German at TestDaF TDN 4 for the Berlin year (the underlying Audio Communication and Technology M.Sc. is taught mainly in German and requires C1 for admission with foreign qualifications)
focus: Electronic Music / Live Electronics; Immersive/Spatial Audio; Electroacoustic Composition; Sonic Arts
whatYouStudy: Signal processing, electroacoustics, room acoustics, music informatics and virtual acoustics on the Berlin side; composition, live electronics, sound art, algorithmic composition and field recording on the Sonology side. Year 1 requires 39 ECTS of mandatory modules plus 21 ECTS of electives from the Audio Communication and Technology programme. Built on a long-standing collaboration on electroacoustic music and sound spatialisation.
entryRequirements: Bachelor's, master's or equivalent degree in science, engineering, humanities, social sciences, artistic-scientific, business or legal fields; engineering-level mathematics (Analysis I, Linear Algebra); knowledge of a programming language or computer algebra system; English IELTS 6.0/TOEFL 83; German TDN 4 (C1 stated for the parent M.Sc.). Numerus clausus applies to the parent programme.
acceptsNonMusic: Yes — a technical degree is in fact the expected background. The parent programme's requirement is "a bachelor's, master's or graduate degree in a science, engineering, humanities or social sciences" field, with demonstrated higher mathematics and programming. His BSc Software Engineering fits better here than at any conservatory.
portfolioSpec: A research project proposal is required with the application. No music portfolio requirement is published for the TU Berlin side — UNVERIFIED whether the Sonology side requires a separate creative portfolio.
auditionSpec: None published on the TU Berlin page; selection is document- and proposal-based. Confirm whether the Institute of Sonology runs its own admission interview for year 2.
applicationOpens: UNVERIFIED
deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date: 15 February (as published for the current year). Programme starts in October.
tuitionIntl: TU Berlin charges no tuition — only the compulsory semester fee (social contribution plus public-transport ticket). In year 2 the Royal Conservatoire's regular tuition fees apply (Dutch statutory non-EU rate — amount UNVERIFIED). Travel, accommodation and living costs are the student's own.
scholarship: DAAD Study Scholarships – Master Studies for All Academic Disciplines (Tunisia eligible); Deutschlandstipendium; Erasmus+ mobility support for the Hague year — UNVERIFIED.
facilities: TU Berlin's Audio Communication group (electroacoustics, virtual acoustics, spatial audio labs) plus the Institute of Sonology in The Hague — one of the historic centres of electronic music, with major studio and spatialisation infrastructure.
fitNotes: Intellectually the strongest technical-artistic hybrid available to a software engineer, and nearly free on the Berlin side. But it is engineering-heavy (Analysis I and Linear Algebra prerequisites, C1-level German for the parent programme) and produces spatial-audio researchers and electroacoustic composers, not DJs. Worth listing because his CS degree is an asset here rather than a liability. Note: the plain TU Berlin "Audio Communication and Technology" M.Sc. is the same entry route without the Sonology year.

program: Professional Media Creation (M.A.)
university: SAE Institute Germany (mandatory modules in Bochum; electives at all German SAE campuses incl. Berlin) — degree awarded by Folkwang Universität der Künste
city: Bochum (electives across Berlin, Hamburg, Cologne, Munich, Frankfurt, Stuttgart, Leipzig, Hannover, Nürnberg)
institutionType: Private specialist audio/media academy in partnership with a public art university
degree: M.A. (Master of Arts), awarded by Folkwang Universität der Künste
durationEcts: 2 years (4 semesters) / 120 ECTS
focus: Music Production; Sound Design; Recording/Engineering; Sonic Arts (project-based, cross-media)
whatYouStudy: Project-based artistic master spanning music, film, video art, installation, sound art, photography and game art. Core modules: artistic practice, project planning, narration, contract law, marketing, event management. Elective modules cover audio, video, multimedia and lighting, plus perceptual psychology, design, real-time systems and media history. Mandatory modules run as weekend blocks in Bochum, so part-time employment alongside is feasible. Delivered with Folkwang's ICEM (Institute for Computer Music and Electronic Media).
entryRequirements: A professionally qualifying higher-education degree (berufsqualifizierender Hochschulabschluss) with a minimum of 180 ECTS, plus demonstration of artistic aptitude.
acceptsNonMusic: Yes. The only degree condition published is a "berufsqualifizierender Hochschulabschluss" with at least 180 ECTS — no subject restriction. A software-engineering BSc qualifies formally; admission then rests on the artistic project proposal.
portfolioSpec: A written artistic project proposal, plus previous creative work reviewed at the colloquium. Number/length of works not specified — UNVERIFIED.
auditionSpec: No performance audition. Selection is by colloquium with SAE and Folkwang representatives, reviewing the project concept and the applicant's previous creative work.
applicationOpens: UNVERIFIED
deadline: UNVERIFIED — no deadline published; intake is every October. Contact SAE Bochum admissions.
tuitionIntl: Self-pay: €400 enrolment fee, then either 24 monthly instalments of €485 (≈€11,640) or 4 semester payments of €2,838 (€11,352). Total roughly €11,750–€12,040.
scholarship: None found for non-EU students. The award is a Folkwang (state university) degree, so DAAD Study Scholarships may in principle be usable — UNVERIFIED for a private-provider delivery model; check with DAAD before relying on it.
facilities: SAE's German campuses are equipped audio/studio facilities (SAE is one of the largest audio-education networks worldwide); elective modules can also be taken at Folkwang University and its ICEM computer-music institute. Specific console/room detail UNVERIFIED.
fitNotes: A genuine accredited master (state Folkwang degree) with no audition and no subject restriction — the most accessible formal qualification on this list. Downsides: German-only, ~€12,000 self-pay, weekend-block format in Bochum rather than a music capital, and a broad cross-media rather than music-production focus. Reasonable insurance policy, not a first choice.

program: Medienkunst/Mediengestaltung (Media Art and Design) – M.F.A.
university: Bauhaus-Universität Weimar, Faculty of Art and Design
institutionType: Public art and design university
durationEcts: Standard 2 semesters for applicants holding a bachelor of at least 8 semesters / 240 ECTS; shorter bachelors require additional bridge semesters (so realistically 3–4 semesters for a 180-ECTS BSc)
language: English-language curriculum with some modules taught in German (Interface Design offers a fully English programme). German A2 required; English C1 (TOEFL 95 / IELTS 7.0).
focus: Sonic Arts (practice-based); Electroacoustic Composition; Sound Design (radio/acoustic ecology)
whatYouStudy: Project- and experimentation-driven MFA covering organisation and technology alongside creative, analytical and critical skills. Six professorships shape the sound side: Electroacoustic Composition, Experimental Radio, Acoustic Ecologies, Media Environments, Interface Design and Media Events — an unusually deep concentration of sound chairs in one art faculty. Applicants define a planned master topic in advance.
entryRequirements: Bachelor of Fine Arts in Media Art and Design or an equivalent first university degree recognised as professionally relevant; German A2; English C1 (TOEFL ≥95 or IELTS 7.0); passed aptitude test; motivation letter of about one A4 page setting out the desired study focus and planned master topic. Applications go through the Bauhaus.CampusPortal, NOT uni-assist.
acceptsNonMusic: Check. The requirement is a BFA in Media Art and Design "or equivalent first university degree recognized as professionally relevant" — relevance is judged case by case on the portfolio, so a software-engineering BSc with a strong media-art portfolio is arguable but not guaranteed. The 240-ECTS expectation is a second hurdle.
portfolioSpec: "Artistic portfolio, i.e. a compilation of own artistic/creative works" as a PDF of max 20 MB, plus links to hosted interactive or time-based works where applicable. Plus a ~1 page motivation letter naming the planned master topic. No fixed number of works.
auditionSpec: Aptitude test, portfolio-based, with a possible personal interview. No live audition. Results announced 6–8 weeks after the deadline.
applicationOpens: 2 February (aptitude-test registration opens)
deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date: applications close 31 March; enrolment deadline 30 September; winter-semester start only.
tuitionIntl: "No, there are no tuition fees, however enrolled students must pay a semester contribution fee." Contribution amount UNVERIFIED. Thuringia charges no non-EU tuition.
scholarship: DAAD Study Scholarships – Master Studies for Artists (Fine Art/Design/Film strand), Tunisia eligible; Deutschlandstipendium
facilities: Bauhaus heritage institution; the Experimental Radio and Electroacoustic Composition chairs run their own studios and broadcast infrastructure. Specific equipment detail UNVERIFIED.
fitNotes: Rare combination: tuition-free, largely English-taught, portfolio-only admission, and a real cluster of sound professorships. But the English bar is high (IELTS 7.0 — well above the IELTS 6.0 most programmes ask), the 240-ECTS assumption may force bridge semesters, and the output is sound art/experimental radio rather than production. A credible second-tier target if he can hit IELTS 7.

program: Mediale Künste (Media Arts) – Diplom 2, postgraduate (MFA-equivalent), with Klangkunst / Sound focus
university: Kunsthochschule für Medien Köln (KHM)
institutionType: Public art school (media arts academy)
degree: Diplom 2 (postgraduate diploma; the KHM states it is internationally comparable to an M.F.A.)
durationEcts: 4 semesters (postgraduate track); ECTS not published — UNVERIFIED
language: German (most instruction in German; A2 certificate at application, B2 at enrolment)
focus: Sonic Arts (practice-based); Sound Design; Electronic Music
whatYouStudy: Free, project-based artistic study: students choose and combine their own artistic focal points, supervised across disciplines by professors and technical staff. Klangkunst (sound art) is one of the available specialisations, delivered through the KHM's Klanglabor — project-oriented practice combined with current sound discourse via seminars, lectures, practical exercises and work presentations. The centre of the degree is the student's individually developed artistic project.
entryRequirements: General higher-education entrance qualification (Abitur-equivalent) plus a completed higher-education degree in a relevant area of study. Alternative route: entrance qualification plus at least two years of professional artistic/creative practice. German A2 at application, B2 (Goethe-Institut) at enrolment. For Diplom 2, an outline for a potential project must be produced.
acceptsNonMusic: Yes — computer science is named as a relevant prior field. The accepted areas include "IT and engineering sciences" (German listing: "Informatik, Fotoingenieurwesen" among others alongside theatre/film/TV studies, literature, art and cultural studies, communication design, visual communication). His BSc Software Engineering is directly in scope.
portfolioSpec: Samples of artistic/design work — "videos, films, photographs, computer graphics, animations, drawings, texts, compositions, and music videos". For Diplom 2 additionally an outline for a potential project, typically 2–3 pages of text or sketches with explanations.
auditionSpec: No multi-stage examination. A commission evaluates the submitted work samples; artistic suitability as shown in the portfolio is the decisive selection criterion. (Shortlisted applicants are normally interviewed — UNVERIFIED.)
applicationOpens: mid-October
deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date: application period runs from mid-October to January/February; winter-semester start only.
tuitionIntl: No tuition. "Contributions of approx. 400 euros per semester" covering the NRW-wide semester ticket, student union fees and equipment insurance.
scholarship: DAAD Study Scholarships – Master Studies for Artists (Fine Art/Film strand); Deutschlandstipendium; KHM runs its own scholarship/Schaukasten programme for enrolled students — details UNVERIFIED.
facilities: Klanglabor (sound laboratory) and the exMedia Sound area; full media-arts production infrastructure (film, video, computer graphics) in Cologne — Germany's media capital, with the WDR broadcaster and a strong electronic-music history.
fitNotes: Quietly one of the best-fitting options: it explicitly accepts computer-science graduates, admission is decided on a portfolio plus a 2–3 page project outline with no audition, and it costs ~€400 a semester. The trade-offs are German B2 and an art-school framing — he would be making sound art in the Klanglabor rather than learning mixdowns. Good if he wants Cologne, credentials and freedom rather than production drills.

program: Audiovisual Media Creation and Technology (Audiovisuelle Medien) – M.Sc., profile 3D-Audio and Music Technology
university: Hochschule der Medien Stuttgart (HdM)
institutionType: Public university of applied sciences (media)
degree: M.Sc. (some sources list M.Eng. for the German-language variant — confirm which title applies)
durationEcts: 3 semesters / 90 ECTS (50 compulsory + 20 flexible + 20 thesis)
focus: Immersive/Spatial Audio; Sound Design; Recording/Engineering; Music Technology
whatYouStudy: Three profiles: 3D-Audio and Music Technology, Visual Media Creation, and Computer-Generated Imagery. The 3D-Audio and Music Technology profile addresses current questions in audio technology with an explicit focus on 3D audio and its application in sound design, radio drama (Hörspiel) and interactive audio installations, worked through with high practical relevance in modern studios. Research- and leadership-competence oriented.

Proof of German required. Motivation letter (max 2 pages) and letters of recommendation can improve the application ranking by up to 0.5 grade points.

A software-engineering BSc covers the engineering/informatics half (15 ECTS in maths/informatics is easy) but he would need to evidence ~15 ECTS in media/design/sound applications, which his degree probably lacks.

auditionSpec: None. Document- and grade-based admission via the HdM application portal; no audition or on-site test published.
applicationOpens: UNVERIFIED
deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date: 15 July for the winter semester; 15 January for the summer semester. Note one source states winter-semester entry only — confirm.
tuitionIntl: Baden-Württemberg LHGebG applies: €1,500 per semester for non-EU/EEA students (≈€4,500 over 3 semesters). No separate programme tuition.
scholarship: DAAD Study Scholarships – Master Studies for All Academic Disciplines; Deutschlandstipendium
facilities: Modern audio studios used for the 3D-audio work, plus a television studio and full AV production infrastructure. Specific immersive-room/console detail UNVERIFIED.
fitNotes: The best German fit for immersive/3D audio with a technical entry route and no audition — his CS background is an advantage and there is no artistic gatekeeping. Two problems: he probably cannot show the expected media/design ECTS, and it is German-taught in Baden-Württemberg (€1,500/semester). Also engineering-flavoured: 3D audio, Hörspiel and installations, not producing tracks.

program: Masterstudium Computermusik und Klangkunst (MA Computer Music and Sound Art)
university: Kunstuniversität Graz (KUG) — Institute of Electronic Music and Acoustics (IEM)
institutionType: Public university of music and performing arts (art university)
focus: Electronic Music / Live Electronics + Sonic Arts + Immersive/Spatial Audio (computer music)
language: German is the programme language; the admission interview is held in German OR English
durationEcts: 2 years / 4 semesters / 120 ECTS
whatYouStudy: Four intertwined strands: computer music composition; performance and interpretation of electronic works; conception and development of new electronic instruments; and music informatics. Plus history, theory and aesthetics of computer music, and (master level) methods of artistic-scientific research. IEM is one of Europe's leading centres for Ambisonics/spatial audio research and runs its own well-known open-source plug-in suite and multichannel performance spaces; graduates are prepared for music, art, media and the creative industries.
entryRequirements: A completed bachelor's degree; you upload the bachelor diploma and transcript with certified German/English translations. The study dean formally assesses equivalence of the prior degree ("der Studiendekan die Gleichwertigkeit des Vorstudiums prüfen kann"). The curriculum names a BA in Computermusik or in Komposition und Musiktheorie (or an equivalent degree from a recognised post-secondary institution) as the reference qualification, and the admission colloquium can prescribe up to 20 ECTS of bachelor elective catch-up courses where skills are missing.
portfolioSpec: Two meaningful examples of your own artistic work ("zwei aussagekräftige Beispiele deiner künstlerischen Arbeit"), approx. 5 minutes each, as audio or video documents. Multichannel material must be reduced to stereo. Total upload not more than approx. 150 MB, uploaded before the registration deadline. Works may be compositions with electroacoustic means, sound installations, documentation of performances/interpretations of computer-music works, development of computer-music instruments, or music-informatics applications.
auditionSpec: No live/on-site audition. The exam is a colloquium/interview held via Zoom in German or English, discussing the submitted works, your motivation, interests and intended area of specialisation. No instrument required.
applicationOpens: 1 March (annual)
deadline: Registration 1 March – 1 May; the KUG page currently shows the Zoom interview taking place in June 2027, i.e. the cycle for a September 2027 start. PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date (exact interview day was not published on the page read).
tuitionIntl: €726.72 per semester Studienbeitrag for third-country nationals (Tunisian citizens are third-country nationals), plus €26.20 ÖH student-union fee per semester (2026 rates).
scholarship: None found specific to this programme. KUG operates a tuition-fee waiver for third-country nationals from a defined list of Eastern/South-Eastern European countries — Tunisia is NOT on that list. KUG itself states that financing a degree purely from internal scholarships is barely feasible.
fundingLevel: Partial (low public fee only; no stipend found)
stipend: UNVERIFIED — no stipend attached to admission
facilities: IEM: multichannel/Ambisonics production and performance spaces, electronic-instrument development labs, strong music-informatics research profile; internationally recognised for spatial-audio tooling. Specific room inventory not listed on the pages read (UNVERIFIED in detail).
acceptsNonMusic: Check — leaning No without preparation. The public page only says a bachelor's degree plus equivalence assessment by the study dean; the curriculum names computer music / composition-and-music-theory bachelors as the reference. A software-engineering BSc would be judged on the portfolio plus possible catch-up of up to 20 ECTS of bachelor courses. Realistic only if the two 5-minute works are genuinely strong electronic/computer-music pieces.
fitNotes: The single best European home for serious electronic/computer music and spatial audio, and the admission burden is unusually light: two 5-minute works and a Zoom interview in English — no live instrument audition, no German test for the exam itself. Main obstacle: the degree is taught in German, and the aesthetic centre of gravity is experimental/art computer music, not club-oriented DJ/producer craft.

program: Master Programme Postdigital Lutherie
university: Kunstuniversität Linz (University of Art and Design Linz) in cooperation with Anton Bruckner Privatuniversität
institutionType: Public art university (jointly with a private music university)
focus: Electronic Music / Live Electronics + Sound Design (postdigital musical-instrument design and performance)
language: English — taught entirely in English; "German skills are not required to join the programme"
durationEcts: 4 semesters (2 years); ECTS UNVERIFIED (not stated on the pages read, normally 120)
whatYouStudy: Postdigital musical instruments at the intersection of design & technology, composition & performance, and art/media theory. Students reconnect acoustic, electronic and digital approaches to instrument design in tangible sonic artefacts — building controllers, interfaces and instruments and then composing/performing with them. Hosted by the Media Institute's Tangible Interaction Design lab (tamlab), with the composition/computer-music department of Anton Bruckner Privatuniversität as partner; courses are cross-creditable with the ABPU MA Komposition.
entryRequirements: "A valid bachelor (or equivalent) degree" is required — no field restriction is stated. Applicants who did not graduate in Austria may have to supply additional entrance requirements/legalisations of documents. No German-language requirement.
portfolioSpec: "A portfolio of your works" uploaded during online registration, plus materials to bring/present for the interview. The page does not fix a number of works, a duration or a file format (UNVERIFIED at that level of detail) — contact Univ.-Prof. Dr. Martin Kaltenbrunner (martin.kaltenbrunner@kunstuni-linz.at), who handles the registration procedure.
auditionSpec: Entrance examination in the form of an interview around the submitted portfolio. Whether it is on-site in Linz or remote is not stated on the page (UNVERIFIED) — the 2026/27 entrance exams were scheduled for a single day, 29 June 2026, which implies attendance.
applicationOpens: UNVERIFIED for the 2027 cycle
deadline: For the 2026/27 intake: applications open until 19 June 2026, entrance exams 29 June 2026. PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. Note this is a June deadline, i.e. much later than the usual Oct–Feb window.
tuitionIntl: Free of charge for EU citizens; non-EU citizens currently pay €726.72 per semester (plus the standard ÖH fee). Students can apply to university fee-reduction funds.
scholarship: University fee-reduction funds are mentioned on the admission page; no named external scholarship found (amounts and eligibility UNVERIFIED).
fundingLevel: Partial (very low fee; fee-reduction funds may apply)
facilities: tamlab (Tangible Interaction Design laboratory) inside the Media Institute; access to Anton Bruckner Privatuniversität's electronic-music production and presentation spaces; Linz's Ars Electronica ecosystem sits next door and Kunstuni Linz programmes routinely present work there.
acceptsNonMusic: Yes (best-in-slice on this point). The admission page states only: "To study at Postdigital Lutherie you need a valid bachelor (or equivalent) degree to qualify for the admission to this master programme" — no music degree, no conservatory training and no German is demanded, and the subject matter (building instruments, code, interfaces) directly rewards a software-engineering background.
fitNotes: The most realistically enterable, genuinely hands-on, English-taught, near-free option in Austria for someone with a CS/SE bachelor and no conservatory record — he would be building his own instruments and performing with them. Obstacle: it is instrument-design/performance research, not a DJ/producer or mixing-and-mastering course; he must also confirm the 2027 dates because the cycle closes in June, not February.

program: Masterstudium Tonmeister_in (specialisations: Musikproduktion Klassik / Musikproduktion Popularmusik / Filmton)
university: mdw – Universität für Musik und darstellende Kunst Wien (University of Music and Performing Arts Vienna), Institut für Kompositionsstudien, Ton- und Musikproduktion
institutionType: Public university of music and performing arts
focus: Recording/Engineering + Music Production + Film Sound (Tonmeister)
language: German — proof of German at level B2 is a condition of admission (Goethe-Zertifikat B2, ÖSD B2, or the mdw German test)
durationEcts: 2 years / 4 semesters; ECTS UNVERIFIED on the pages read (curriculum PDF not parsed)
whatYouStudy: Managing complex audio productions end to end — artistic-technical planning, creative realisation, completion — with a large elective share so you sharpen an individual artistic profile within one of three specialisations: classical music production, popular-music production, or film sound. Sound reinforcement and sound design can be taken as additional emphases regardless of specialisation. A master project is central.
entryRequirements: Passed admission examination; a completed subject-relevant bachelor's or diploma degree; proof of German at B2; and proof of unimpaired hearing. The admission info sheet is explicit: you must upload "Nachweis über ein abgeschlossenes Studium (Bachelor o. Diplom) in einem facheinschlägigen Studium Tonmeister_in" — i.e. a Tonmeister-type degree. Also required: a current specialist medical certificate with audiogram (not older than two months) confirming physiologically unimpaired hearing across 125–8,000 Hz.
portfolioSpec: Very heavy and fully specified. (a) Motivation video, max 3 minutes, answering a fixed question list for your specialisation. (b) Instrument/voice video: for Popularmusik, 2 jazz/popular works with improvisation or ad libs (an own composition is allowed; for piano, one piece may be improvisation using keyboards/synths/DAWs such as Ableton Live with clearly audible playing craft and own sound design); band or play-alongs permitted; total video duration max 15 minutes. (c) Piano video if piano is not your main instrument. (d) PORTFOLIO — Popularmusik: SIX popular-music productions in different styles, produced, recorded and mixed substantially by you, at least three with vocals and at least two involving recording of acoustic instruments, all delivered as stereo audio (5.1/Dolby Atmos versions optional), each at least 2:30 and max 30 minutes in total, plus written documentation of 7,000–12,000 characters (approach, microphone choices, session photos, DAW screenshots, challenges, critical reflection). Klassik: three music-recording projects, two pure stereo audio productions with different ensembles plus one free project (audio or video, stereo/5.1/Dolby Atmos, with a stereo version supplied), total 20–40 minutes, plus the same 7,000–12,000-character documentation. program: Master Son
university: École nationale supérieure Louis-Lumière (ENS Louis-Lumière)
city: Saint-Denis (La Cité du Cinéma), Paris region
degree: Diplôme de niveau Bac+5 conférant le grade de Master (RNCP 41626)
durationEcts: 3 years full-time, entered at Bac+2 level (school recruits at 120 ECTS validated). Per-year ECTS UNVERIFIED.
focus: Recording/Engineering + Film/Game Sound + Sonic Arts + Immersive Audio + some Music Production
institutionType: Public grande école (Ministère de l'Enseignement supérieur, de la Recherche et de l'Espace)
language: French (English taught as a subject 'tout au long du cursus')
whatYouStudy: Year 1 common core on three axes: (1) science/technology — 'acoustique et électroacoustique, traitement du signal, électronique appliquée'; (2) instrumental fundamentals — 'prise de son, montage et mixage pour le cinéma' plus music production, radio creation and live-sound technique; (3) project-based productions with the Master Cinéma cohort and outside partners. Years 2-3 = one of three pathways: SON À L'IMAGE (film, documentary, animation, games, VR, object-based mixing), ARTS SONORES (electroacoustic music, installations, spatial audio, interactive systems), INGÉNIERIE SONORE (live concert reinforcement, system design, venue acoustics). Editing/mixing on Avid and Merging Technologies systems; Wwise + Unity for interactive audio.
entryRequirements: Baccalauréat (or equivalent foreign diploma) AND two validated years of higher education in the same State-recognised formation, equal to 120 ECTS — or an RNCP level-5 (Bac+2) qualification. Age: 'moins de 27 ans au 31 décembre' of the year preceding the concours (2026 cycle: born after 31 Dec 1998). Foreign diplomas must be translated into French by a sworn translator (including English-language diplomas); ENIC-NARIC equivalence attestation may be required. Non-francophone secondary diploma holders must present DELF B2 (or TCF niveau 4 / DALF) at the time of application. International candidates may request permission to use a printed French translation dictionary in the exams.
portfolioSpec: PHASE 1 = dossier, emailed to concoursson@ens-louis-lumiere.fr. Subject released 5 Feb 2026 15:00, due 20 Feb 2026 15:00. Contents: (a) written answers to questions on background and motivation; (b) 'une création sonore d'une durée maximale de 3 min en lien avec une thématique imposée'; (c) 'une analyse comparée à partir de trois extraits de films disponibles en ligne sur une thématique donnée'. Coefficient 1.
auditionSpec: PHASE 2 (written, ON-SITE in Île-de-France, mandatory): 'Épreuve écrite de mathématiques-physique' 1h15 + 'QCM d'électricité-électronique' 1h15. No calculators. Son and Cinéma concours carry an eliminatory-mark system. PHASE 3 (oral, ON-SITE, half a day per candidate): 'Oral d'écoute et d'analyse' 30 min (a short sound piece is played; listening, analysis, imagination assessed); 'Oral de techniques du son' 30 min (technical discussion, 'des questions pratiques, impliquant la manipulation de matériel, peuvent également être posées'); 'Oral de culture générale et de motivation' 30 min. 16 admitted per Master per year.
acceptsNonMusic: YES — no music degree, no conservatoire diploma and no audition on an instrument. The published condition is only 'deux années d'études supérieures dans une même formation ... reconnue par l'État et égales à 120 crédits ECTS'. The Master Son référentiel is explicitly technical/scientific ('Notions générales d'informatique', 'Notions de matériel informatique', electricity-electronics, maths/physics) plus 'Culture cinématographique / Culture musicale / Culture radiophonique' and, under Motivation, 'Parcours antérieur — Expérience et pratique personnelles — Stages dans les domaines du son'. A software-engineering BSc is a genuine advantage on Phase 2.
applicationOpens: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date: 2026 cycle pre-registration opened 1 Dec 2025 at 15:00. Expect early Dec 2026 for the Sept 2027 intake; the Livret de concours is published each late November.
deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. 2026 cycle: pre-registration closed 14 Jan 2026 15:00; fee paid by 21 Jan 2026 15:00; Phase 1 dossier due 20 Feb 2026 15:00; Phase 1 results 24 Mar 2026; Son written test 10 Apr 2026; Son orals 8-12 Jun 2026; final admission list mid-July 2026.
tuitionIntl: €300 annual registration in 2025-2026 + CVEC ~€105. 'La scolarité est gratuite pour les 150 étudiant·e·s, hors frais d'inscription annuels (300€ en 2025-2026).' No differentiated non-EU fee published. Concours entry fee €120 (€60 for CROUS scholarship holders).
fundingLevel: Partial (tuition effectively free; no stipend attached)
scholarship: CROUS bourse sur critères sociaux if eligible; France Excellence Eiffel is possible in principle but must be nominated by the institution — UNVERIFIED whether ENS Louis-Lumière nominates. No programme-specific scholarship found.
stipend: No stipend. Living costs in the Paris region are the candidate's own. UNVERIFIED.
facilities: Based at La Cité du Cinéma, Saint-Denis (Luc Besson's studio complex) since 2012. Avid and Merging Technologies audio post systems; Wwise/Unity; three specialised pathways with studio, live-sound and immersive/spatial facilities. Founded 1926 under Louis Lumière and Léon Gaumont. Applied-research projects; only 150 students total across the three Masters. Teaching staff publish concours preparation material (autopscience.com, informatique-audio-electronique.over.blog).
fitNotes: The single best public-sector fit in France for this profile: near-zero tuition, an entrance exam whose written half (maths, physics, electricity, electronics, computing notions) plays directly to a software-engineering degree, and no music-degree prerequisite. The obstacles are the 3-min original sound creation for Phase 1 (he must build a real recording/editing/mixing practice in 2026), the compulsory on-site written and oral rounds in Île-de-France (three separate trips), the DELF B2 certificate, and the age cap of 27. Career emphasis is film/live/arts sonores rather than club-oriented DJ/producer work — he would get world-class craft, not electronic-dance-music career coaching.

program: Diplôme de La Fémis — Département SON (via the Concours international, reserved for non-EEA nationals)
university: La Fémis — École nationale supérieure des métiers de l'image et du son
degree: Diplôme de La Fémis conférant le grade de Master (RNCP niveau 7)
durationEcts: 4 years full-time ('cursus principal'). ECTS UNVERIFIED.
focus: Film Sound (production sound, editing, mixing, sound design for cinema)
institutionType: Public national film school (Ministère de la Culture / CNC)
language: French only — 'La maîtrise de la langue française est obligatoire. Les épreuves se déroulent en français, de même que les enseignements dispensés à l'École.'

Detailed module list not published on the pages read — UNVERIFIED. The concours syllabus signals the content: cinema culture, professions and equipment, 'esthétique sonore et culture musicale', and applied science (acoustic units, periodic phenomena, Fourier, microphones/amplifiers/loudspeakers, impedance, hearing and loudness, Fechner's law, Fletcher diagram, DC/AC and Ohm's law).
entryRequirements: Concours international is open only to nationals of countries outside the EEA, Andorra, Monaco and Switzerland — a Tunisian national must use this route (dual nationals of those states must take the concours général). 'Les candidats doivent être âgés de moins de 27 ans au 1er janvier' of the concours year; must hold the equivalent of a baccalauréat AND have validated at least two successive years of higher education (by equivalence), with certified translations of diplomas. A 'professionnel' route exists: under 30, baccalauréat, and at least two years of professional activity in ANY sector. French: for non-nationals of francophone states, a certificate from a French-government-approved body attesting CEFR B1 minimum, or a copy of a higher-education diploma obtained in a francophone cursus. Maximum three attempts at any Fémis concours.
portfolioSpec: First round, all submitted by 12 Feb 2026 12:00 via the candidate space (anonymised — no name anywhere, including in audio/video files or credits): (1) 'dossier personnel d'enquête' max 20 pages on an imposed theme — written part max 10 pages (font ≥10, numbered) + visual part max 10 pages, optionally illustrated by a video document max 5 min AND/OR a sound document max 5 min (links on page 1 via an anonymous account); (2) 'note de synthèse' summarising the dossier, max 1 A4 page; (3) 'lettre de présentation et motivation' explaining the path taken and why cinema, why La Fémis and why the chosen department, max 1 A4 page; (4) 'un portfolio de projets personnels : 3 projets au maximum, sur 8 pages au maximum, au format PDF' — accepted: photos, drawings, screenplay, comics, video (viewing link in the PDF), 'son (via un lien d'écoute indiqué sur le PDF)'; total running time of moving image or sound limited to 3 minutes.
auditionSpec: First round also includes, remotely by videoconference: a film-analysis test (25 Feb 2026, 3 hours, extract screened 3 times, candidate records a 5-8 minute spoken analysis; coefficient 1) and the DEPARTMENTAL SON tests (24-26 Feb 2026, coefficient 2): (a) written paper 1h30 on cinema culture, sound aesthetics, musical culture and the science list above — 'C'est uniquement la « compréhension », le « principe » des notions énumérées ci-dessus, qui sont pris en compte'; (b) oral 30 min in which 'les jurés pourront revenir sur l'épreuve écrite, et interrogeront le ou la candidat·e sur son parcours et ses motivations'. Max 14 candidates declared admissible across all seven departments. SECOND ROUND: one public oral interview in PARIS, max 30 min, coefficient 4, between 15 and 26 June 2026, covering culture, tastes, experience and projects, the earlier tests and the submitted portfolio/letters. Max 7 admitted in total, jury balancing across departments.
acceptsNonMusic: YES for the diploma requirement — only 'l'équivalent d'un baccalauréat' plus two successive years of higher education in any field is required, and the alternative 'professionnel' route accepts two years of work experience 'quel que soit le secteur d'activité'. No music or audio qualification is demanded. BUT the son written paper tests cinema culture, sound aesthetics AND musical culture, so the gap is cultural, not formal.
applicationOpens: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date: 2026 cycle online registration opened Tuesday 9 December 2025 at 12:00.
deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. 2026 cycle: registration closed 9 Jan 2026 12:00; documents due 12 Feb 2026 12:00; departmental tests 24-26 Feb 2026; film analysis 25 Feb 2026; admissibility list 2 Apr 2026; oral 15-26 Jun 2026; admitted list 26 Jun 2026.

Before 24 April a sworn declaration of ability to pay the €8,000 is required as a financial guarantee; admitted candidates must provide, before early July, an attestation of full coverage for the whole four years — 'qui pourra notamment être délivrée par l'Ambassade de France pour les bénéficiaires d'une bourse'.
