"All genres and forms of expression" welcome. RMC runs technology labs for electronic music and multimedia projects plus recording studios. Approx. eight students admitted per year.
entryRequirements: Completed bachelor's in music from RMC, another Danish conservatory or a foreign institution, or expected completion by 1 July of the entry year. "Based on a specific assessment, the conservatory may recognise other artistically based Bachelor's degrees." English test requirement for non-EU applicants: UNVERIFIED. Application fee DKK 600 (non-refundable).
acceptsNonMusic: CHECK - realistically No for a pure software-engineering BSc. The only opening is: "Based on a specific assessment, the conservatory may recognise other artistically based Bachelor's degrees." A BSc Software Engineering is not an artistically based degree, so this is a discretionary long shot he would need to negotiate with RMC directly before applying.
portfolioSpec: Round 1 (portfolio, digital): 2-3 compositions totalling 10 minutes, mp3 format; optional sheet music/notation as PDF; a description of each work of max 500 characters covering the creative process and your specific role; plus documentation of music-related activity over the past three years. Hard rule: "one-third of the music submitted in your portfolio must be composed for and performed by others." All work must be solely your own composition - "co-writes are not permitted." Explicitly stated: "You do not need to participate as a musician/singer in the music examples in your portfolio, and it is not a requirement to be able to play an instrument - we also accept applicants who work exclusively on computers."
auditionSpec: Round 2 is IN PERSON at RMC in Copenhagen, 25 minutes total: a 10-minute presentation of DIFFERENT material (live, recording or hybrid; up to 5 musicians including a sound engineer permitted), a 5-minute contextual presentation of methods and artistic traditions/influences, and a 10-minute interview. Scored on a 100-point scale; minimum 40 points to pass.
tuitionIntl: EUR 10,000 per study year for the Master programme (students from outside EU/EEA). Free for Danish, EU/EEA and Swiss citizens. 2025/26 figures.
scholarship: None found on RMC's own tuition page. Listed fee EXEMPTIONS: participation in Erasmus Mundus, Fulbright or DIS programmes, bilateral agreements, permanent Danish residency (or qualification for it), Ukrainian temporary-residence holders, and certain Afghanistan-related cases. Third-party sources mention Danish Government Scholarships for highly qualified non-EU/EEA students - UNVERIFIED on RMC pages.
fundingLevel: None verified (self-pay at EUR 10,000/yr unless an exemption route applies)
applicationOpens: 16 December (opened 16 Dec 2025 for the Aug 2026 intake) - PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date; expect mid-December 2026 for a Sept 2027 start
deadline: 3 February 2026 at 12:00 CET - PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. Prior-cycle rhythm: round-1 results 5 March, on-site round 2 on 7-10 April, programme start 17 August.
fitNotes: On CRAFT this is the single best-aligned programme in the Nordics for a computer-based producer: RMC explicitly admits people who "work exclusively on computers" and no instrument is required. The obstacle is the degree gate - it wants a music bachelor, and the one-third "composed for and performed by others" rule plus a no-co-writes rule will be hard to satisfy from a self-taught DJ/producer portfolio. Also budget for a trip to Copenhagen: round 2 is on-site, not online.

program: Master of Music (cand. musicae), Music Performance
university: Rhythmic Music Conservatory (Rytmisk Musikkonservatorium, RMC)
institutionType: Conservatory (state conservatoire under the Danish Ministry of Culture)
durationEcts: 2 years / 120 ECTS, full-time with compulsory attendance
language: Primarily Danish; entrance examination can be conducted in English if you do not speak Danish. Full-degree English delivery: UNVERIFIED
focus: Electronic Music / Live Electronics / Performance (artist-producer path; all genres including electronic)
whatYouStudy: Artist-led two-year performance master built around your own artistic practice, an industry-facing external module and a concluding master's project presented publicly. The page states "All genres and styles are welcome" and "All genres and musical expressions are welcome", and electronic elements and samples are explicitly permitted in submissions. RMC's technology labs (electronic music, multimedia) and recording studios are available.
entryRequirements: Bachelor's degree in music, or expected completion by 1 July of the entry year. You must appear "as a singer or instrumentalist and be artistically responsible for the music", though other roles supporting your artistic vision may be accepted on individual assessment. Application fee DKK 600.
acceptsNonMusic: CHECK - No as published; a music bachelor is required, with discretionary recognition of "other artistically based Bachelor's degrees" only. A software-engineering BSc would be an exception case requiring direct negotiation with RMC.
portfolioSpec: Round 1: 2-3 music examples ON VIDEO (mp4), total duration 10 minutes, showing "a live situation - with or without an audience". Videos must be "one-takes from a fixed camera ... without post-production". Supporting material: sheet music / graphic notation / text as PDF, plus supplementary descriptions of max 500 characters per example.
auditionSpec: Round 2 IN PERSON at RMC, 25 minutes total: a 10-minute concert with minimum one and maximum four other people, a 5-minute presentation of your methods, and a 10-minute interview. Prior cycle held 7-10 April.
tuitionIntl: EUR 10,000 per study year for non-EU/EEA students (Master level). Free for EU/EEA/Swiss.
scholarship: None found on RMC pages; same exemption list as other RMC programmes (Erasmus Mundus, Fulbright, DIS, bilateral agreements, Danish permanent residency).
applicationOpens: 16 December (16 Dec 2025 for the Aug 2026 intake) - PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date
deadline: 3 February 2026 at 12:00 CET - PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date
fitNotes: Genuinely open to electronic/DJ-style live practice, and the live-performance framing suits someone who wants to perform, not just produce. But the fixed-camera, no-post-production one-take video requirement is brutal for a studio producer, and the requirement to be artistically responsible AS a performer is a stricter bar than RMC's Music Creation route. If he applies to RMC, Music Creation is the better door; keep this as the second choice on the same application cycle.

program: Master of Music (MMus) in Tonmeister / Sound Engineer (Tonemester)
university: The Royal Danish Academy of Music (Det Kongelige Danske Musikkonservatorium, DKDM / RDAM)
institutionType: Conservatory (state conservatoire)
durationEcts: 2 years. 120 ECTS is the standard for a Danish MMus but is not restated on the programme page - treat the ECTS figure as UNVERIFIED.
language: English. RDAM states its programmes are taught in English; Danish proficiency is required only for Music Teaching, Aural Training and Music Theory programmes.
focus: Recording / Engineering + Music Production (both rhythmic/pop-rock-jazz and classical)
whatYouStudy: Principal study is music production and recording techniques, organised in close collaboration with the Danish Broadcasting Corporation (DR). Alongside: aural studies, basic piano, music theory and music history. Semester projects, set productions, studio recordings, CD recordings, film sound design and PA work for performances. Students can specialise by genre, sector, producer role or sound-technician role. "Well-equipped studios and plenty of mobile equipment." Study trips, masterclasses, company visits and listening tests.
entryRequirements: Bachelor as Tonemester from DKDM, or Bachelor as Tonemester or equivalent from a Danish music conservatory, or Bachelor as Tonemester or equivalent from a higher education institution abroad at a level corresponding to DKDM. External applicants must sit an entrance examination in addition to holding the musical bachelor exam. RDAM's general prerequisites page states a "Bachelor's degree in music ... or equivalent from a higher education institution abroad at a level equivalent to RDAM".
acceptsNonMusic: NO. The published requirement is a Tonmeister bachelor or an equivalent conservatory-level music degree. A BSc Software Engineering does not meet this and no discretionary clause is offered on the pages read. This is the best-fitting curriculum in the whole slice and the hardest gate - he would need a music/audio bachelor or a documented equivalent first.
portfolioSpec: Two musical production examples, EACH at least 7 minutes: one from the rhythmic genres (pop/rock/jazz) and one from classical music. Non-EU/EEA applicants must ADDITIONALLY submit a production plan documenting the creative process - timeline, equipment/software used, roles of participants and the recording context. (The certified audiogram, max 1 year old, is a Bachelor-level requirement, not master.)
auditionSpec: Principal-study audition of approximately 30 minutes including assessment, built around a roughly 20-minute discussion of the submitted works plus theoretical and practical questions on your "technical and musical standpoint". EU/EEA applicants audition IN PERSON; non-EU/EEA applicants audition ONLINE, with a possible additional interview covering piano, ear training/solfege and theory. Graded on the Danish 7-point scale; decision based on documentation of previous education plus evaluation of the submitted productions.
tuitionIntl: EUR 11,100 per academic year for the Tonmeister/Sound Engineer MASTER (non-EU/EEA), paid in two instalments: 1 June (new students) and 1 September. Free for EU/EEA. For comparison the master fee table runs EUR 11,000-14,900 across specialisations.
scholarship: None found on RDAM pages. Exemptions may exist under Danish national law and must be documented by the applicant (contact admission@dkdm.dk).
applicationOpens: UNVERIFIED (portal opening date not published on the pages read)
deadline: 1 December for both EU/EEA and non-EU/EEA applicants at Master level - PRIOR CYCLE date pattern, confirm the 2027-intake date. RDAM aims to answer non-EU/EEA Bachelor and Master applicants about six weeks after the deadline.
fitNotes: Content-wise this is the classic Nordic recording/production master - DR collaboration, real studios, both rhythmic and classical production, and non-EU applicants audition online so no travel cost. The deal-breaker is entry: it presumes a Tonmeister bachelor. Also note the portfolio demands a CLASSICAL production of 7+ minutes, which a DJ/electronic producer will not have. Realistic only after a bridging audio-engineering bachelor.

program: MSc in Medialogy - specialisation in Sound and Music Computing
university: Aalborg University (AAU)
institutionType: Public university
durationEcts: 2 years / 120 ECTS (4 semesters)
focus: Immersive / Spatial Audio and Sound Design (engineering-side sound and music computing)
whatYouStudy: A creative interdisciplinary programme combining engineering, design, music performance, psycho-acoustics, signal processing and computer science. Content covered across the SMC track: sound processing, music perception and cognition, New Interfaces for Musical Expression; a Sonic Interaction project semester with courses in Embodied Interaction, Sound and Music Signal Analysis, and Physical Models for Sound Synthesis. First-semester electives include Sound and Music Perception and Cognition; after semester 1 you choose whether to continue in Medialogy or specialise in Sound and Music Computing. AAU's problem-based learning means every semester is built around a group project. Industry destinations named by AAU: Bang & Olufsen, T-Rex Engineering, IO Interactive, Carl Martin, Dicentia. NOTE: the standalone MSc in Engineering "Sound and Music Computing" was CLOSED FOR ADMISSION FROM 2024 and replaced by this specialisation inside Medialogy.
entryRequirements: A bachelor's degree in a qualifying area - the published list includes BSc Medialogy, Datalogi (computer science), Software and various engineering-related fields; "Applicants with other backgrounds will receive individual evaluation by the Study Board of Media Technology." Documented English proficiency required. Non-EU applicants must also submit final documentation by 15 June.
acceptsNonMusic: YES - this is the one programme in the slice built for his exact background. Qualifying bachelors explicitly include "BSc Medialogy, Datalogi, Software, and various engineering-related fields", and "Applicants with other backgrounds will receive individual evaluation by the Study Board of Media Technology." No music degree, no music theory and no audition are demanded.
portfolioSpec: None published. Admission is on academic transcripts plus English proficiency documentation - no portfolio of works is requested on the pages read.
auditionSpec: None - no audition, no on-site test.
tuitionIntl: DKK 57,850 per SEMESTER (approx. EUR 7,745) for engineering/technical programmes, i.e. roughly EUR 15,490 per year. Payment due 1 August for the autumn semester. Full refund before study start, 75% within the first month, none thereafter (visa delays excepted).
scholarship: AAU awards approximately 15 scholarships per year consisting of a full TUITION WAIVER plus a monthly stipend of DKK 11,225 (approx. EUR 1,503). All non-EU applicants are automatically considered - no separate application.
fundingLevel: Full (competitive - approx. 15 awards per year university-wide); otherwise self-pay
stipend: Full tuition waiver + DKK 11,225 per month (approx. EUR 1,503) for scholarship holders
applicationOpens: Portal opens mid-December; up to 3 prioritised programme choices allowed
deadline: 15 January, 23:59 CET for non-EU/EEA fee-paying applicants (September intake), decisions 10 April. EU/EEA deadline is 1 March. PRIOR CYCLE pattern - for a Sept 2027 start expect 15 January 2027; confirm when the portal opens in December 2026.
fitNotes: The realistic fully-funded Nordic option for him: his BSc Software Engineering is directly qualifying, there is no audition or portfolio, and the ~15 AAU scholarships give a genuine tuition-waiver-plus-stipend path with automatic consideration. The honest caveat is that this is sound and music COMPUTING - signal processing, synthesis models, sonic interaction, C++/Python-style project work - not DJing, mixing records or A&R. It builds him into an audio developer or technical sound designer. Best used as the funded safety net alongside one or two craft-focused applications.

program: Master's Programme in Performance - Music Production (Masterprogram i musik: musiker, musikproduktion)
university: Royal College of Music in Stockholm (Kungl. Musikhogskolan, KMH)
institutionType: Conservatory / public university college of music
degree: Master of Fine Arts in Music (konstnarlig master)
durationEcts: 2 years / 120 ECTS (hogskolepoang), full-time
language: SWEDISH. The programme page states Swedish is the primary teaching language and the entrance examination is conducted in Swedish; the entrance-test page repeats: "Please note that test is in Swedish as Swedish is the main language for the Master's programme."
focus: Music Production (including music for TV, film, games and interactive media)
whatYouStudy: "Advanced sound and music production focusing on production planning, composition, arranging and orchestration, recording, mixing and mastering." Course spine: Musikproduktion 1 & 2 (theory plus practical work, with seminars in design and communication theory, musical leadership, business insight, entrepreneurship, and music law/copyright) and Eget konstnarligt projekt 1 & 2 (self-directed production projects). Artistic-research preparation courses shared with other master's students. Final year includes a 30-credit thesis project: an extensive music production carried out with research methodology. KMH studios; programme contact is Studio Director Peter Schyborger.
entryRequirements: General eligibility for advanced-level (second-cycle) studies; a completed first-cycle degree of at least 180 ECTS, specifically a Bachelor of Fine Arts in Music or a Bachelor in Music Production (180 credits) or equivalent; and a pass in the entrance examination. Application via antagning.se / universityadmissions.se, code KMH-85000.
acceptsNonMusic: NO, effectively. Published wording requires a "Bachelor of Fine Arts in Music or Bachelor in Music Production (180 credits), or equivalent", and the entrance test is held in Swedish. Two independent blockers for a Tunisian software-engineering graduate.
portfolioSpec: Test 1 - Portfolio and presentation (digital): "The portfolio must contain four digital files with music productions of your own." For each production you must document composer, text author and arranger names; the recording and mixing techniques used; the performers; and your work process and tools. Plus a "comprehensive description of yourself: who you are, musical background, areas of musical interests (approx. 500 words)", a CV, and a "description of what you would like to develop during your master studies (approx. 500 words)". Graded 0-25 points, 10 required to pass.
auditionSpec: Test 2 - conversation, ONLINE via Zoom, approximately 30 minutes, with the jury, based on your portfolio material. Conducted in SWEDISH. Assessed 0-25, 10 or above passes. No travel to Stockholm required for the test itself.
tuitionIntl: SEK 264,000 per academic year for non-EU/EEA/Swiss citizens, billed regularly through the studies. Application fee SEK 900 paid via universityadmissions.se. EU/EEA and Swiss citizens pay neither.
scholarship: "KMH offers a limited number of scholarships that cover the entire tuition fee cost to talented master level students." Number of awards, application process and eligibility conditions are NOT published - UNVERIFIED. Fee-paying master's students also receive FAS+ student insurance.
fundingLevel: Full possible but limited and competitive (tuition-only); otherwise self-pay at SEK 264,000/yr
stipend: Tuition-fee coverage only; no living stipend published
applicationOpens: 1 December (opened 1 Dec 2025 for the Aug 2026 intake) - PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date
deadline: 15 January 2026 (final application and priority ranking on antagning.se; code KMH-85000), entrance exams 7-15 March 2026, programme start 31 August 2026 - PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date; expect 1 Dec 2026 to 15 Jan 2027 for a Sept 2027 start
fitNotes: Curriculum is close to ideal - production planning, arranging, recording, mixing, mastering, plus a full-scale production as the thesis, and tuition can in principle be fully waived by a KMH scholarship. But the programme is taught in Swedish AND the audition conversation is in Swedish, which rules it out for him unless he spends a year on Swedish. Worth keeping on a longer 2028/2029 horizon only if he decides to learn Swedish; otherwise deprioritise despite the excellent content.

program: Master's Programme in Composition - Electroacoustic Music (Masterprogram i komposition, elektroakustisk musik)
university: Royal College of Music in Stockholm (Kungl. Musikhogskolan, KMH)
institutionType: Conservatory / public university college of music
degree: Master of Fine Arts in Music (konstnarlig master)
durationEcts: 2 years / 120 ECTS (hogskolepoang), full-time
language: Programme pages are in Swedish and the entrance test material shows no English alternative; entry requires English 6 / English level 2. Language of instruction NOT explicitly stated - UNVERIFIED, assume Swedish-dominant.
focus: Electronic Music / Live Electronics / Sonic Arts (electroacoustic concert music, interactive sound art, live electronics, experimental electronica)
whatYouStudy: Composition studies at KMH focus on "knowledge, experimental investigations and artistic deepening". The electroacoustic specialisation covers electroacoustic concert music, interactive sound art, live electronics and experimental electronica. Students get access to well-equipped studios and concert halls to present newly composed music, often together with students from other specialisations or in collaboration with professional musical life. Roughly 4 students admitted per year for autumn entry.
entryRequirements: General eligibility for advanced-level studies; an artistic bachelor's degree in music (180 ECTS); English 6 or English level 2; and a passing score on the mandatory entrance audition. Application code KMH-29000.
acceptsNonMusic: NO as published - "an artistic bachelor's degree in music (180 ECTS)" is required. No discretionary clause found on the pages read.
portfolioSpec: Prov 1 (work sample): THREE different compositions, maximum 30 minutes total, all composed within the last three years - "Arbetsprovets ska bestaa av tre olika kompositioner som ger en tydlig bild av din konstnarlig praktik". Accepted formats: scores as PDF, audio as AIFF/WAV/MP3, digital representations, video as MPEG-4 for audiovisual works, and single-page PDF documentation for sound installations. Accompanying single PDF must contain: project description (max 300 words), bullet-point CV (max 300 words), artist statement (max 200 words), motivation for applying (max 200 words) and individual work descriptions (max 50 words each). Work sample due 26 January in the prior cycle.
auditionSpec: Prov 2, conducted ONLINE/at distance: a composition test of 4-8 hours based on materials provided to you, plus a jury interview of approximately 15 minutes. Prior cycle held 7-15 March. No English-language alternative for the test is mentioned.
tuitionIntl: SEK 264,000 per academic year for non-EU/EEA/Swiss citizens; SEK 900 application fee. Free for EU/EEA/Swiss.
scholarship: "KMH offers a limited number of scholarships that cover the entire tuition fee cost to talented master level students." Details UNVERIFIED.
fundingLevel: Full possible but limited and competitive (tuition-only); otherwise self-pay
stipend: Tuition-fee coverage only; no living stipend published
applicationOpens: 1 December (1 Dec 2025 for the Aug 2026 intake) - PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date
deadline: 15 January 2026 on antagning.se (code KMH-29000); work sample by 26 January 2026; on-site/online auditions 7-15 March 2026 - PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date
fitNotes: Strong for someone who wants live electronics and experimental electronica with world-class studios, and the online 4-8 hour composition test avoids travel. But it is an art-music composition track, not a route to club/dance production, it demands three finished compositions from the last three years, it requires an artistic music bachelor, and the working language is Swedish. Poor match for his stated DJ/producer goal - list it only as an ambition-stretch option.

program: Experimental Composition and Creation - Master of Fine Arts in Music with Specialisation in Composition (K2KMP)
university: University of Gothenburg - Academy of Music and Drama (Hogskolan for scen och musik)
institutionType: Public university / academy of music and drama
degree: Master of Fine Arts in Music (MFA), specialisation Composition
durationEcts: 2 years / 120 ECTS
focus: Sonic Arts / Electronic Music (practice-based composition and creation)
whatYouStudy: The programme spans "instrumental and vocal music, sound art, performance and sound installation, electronic and free improvised music". Students pursue an individual explorative project while engaging with visiting experts and collaborating ensembles. Small cohort: only 8-10 students admitted. GU also states that composition students share studios and courses in electronic music and sound art with the music and sound production programme in the professional studio environment at Brewhouse (Gothenburg's music-industry hub) - this statement appears on GU's music overview page rather than the programme page.
entryRequirements: Bachelor's degree in Fine Arts or equivalent; demonstrated musical knowledge and skills assessed via admission tests; English proficiency at English 6 / B level or an equivalent international test score.
acceptsNonMusic: CHECK - unlikely. Requirement is a "Bachelor's degree in Fine Arts or equivalent" plus admission tests. A BSc Software Engineering is not a fine-arts degree, so admission would hinge entirely on the "or equivalent" assessment and on test performance. Treat as a long shot.
portfolioSpec: Applicants must submit "a description of your idea" - an explorative project proposal - with the application, which together with the admission tests forms the basis for selection. The exact media, number of works, durations and file formats are NOT published on the programme page - UNVERIFIED. Request the provbeskrivning from the Academy.
auditionSpec: Admission tests are referenced but their format (on-site vs remote, content, duration) is NOT published on the page read - UNVERIFIED.
tuitionIntl: Full education cost SEK 566,000 for the whole programme, with a first instalment of SEK 141,500. EU/EEA citizens and holders of a Swedish residence permit pay no fees.
scholarship: None found on the programme page - UNVERIFIED
fundingLevel: UNVERIFIED (no programme-level funding found; self-pay SEK 566,000 total)
applicationOpens: 1 December (opened 1 Dec 2025 for the Aug 2026 start)
deadline: CRITICAL SCHEDULING ISSUE: the programme "accepts new students every two years". The 1 Dec 2025 - 15 Jan 2026 window was for the August 2026 - June 2028 cohort, and GU's application page states the next opening is DECEMBER 2027 for an AUTUMN 2028 start. There is therefore NO September 2027 intake. PRIOR CYCLE - confirm with the Academy, but plan around autumn 2028.
fitNotes: English-taught, tiny cohort, real electronic-music and sound-art studio access at Brewhouse - attractive on paper and one of very few English-taught Swedish options in this field. Two hard problems: the biennial intake means it cannot serve a September 2027 start (next is autumn 2028), and it wants a fine-arts bachelor. Note it as a 2028 target and ask the Academy in autumn 2026 whether the "or equivalent" clause could cover an engineering degree plus a strong portfolio.

program: Master's Programme in Music (Konstnarligt masterprogram i musik) - Composition: Music for Film and Media (Komposition - Musik for film och media)
university: Malmo Academy of Music (Musikhogskolan i Malmo), Lund University
institutionType: Public university / academy of music (Faculty of Fine and Performing Arts, Lund University)
degree: Master of Fine Arts in Music (konstnarlig master)
durationEcts: 2 years. 120 ECTS is the standard for a Swedish konstnarligt masterprogram but is not restated on the admission page - treat as UNVERIFIED.
language: UNVERIFIED - the admission pages are in Swedish and the final interview is held on site at the Academy; confirm whether the programme can be followed in English.
focus: Film / Game Sound and applied composition (scoring for film and media)
whatYouStudy: Composition and production of music for film and media: writing, orchestrating and MIXING original scores to picture. The admission process itself indicates the working method - composing a theme and scoring an assigned film clip, delivering lead sheet, audio and video. Malmo's composition studio is described by third-party programme listings as "the programme's platform for students' creative work in electroacoustic music, live electronics, and experimental studio production" - AGGREGATOR-SOURCED, not confirmed on a Lund page, so treat as UNVERIFIED. A separate general Composition specialisation and a Composition Diploma also exist at Malmo.
entryRequirements: "Grundlaggande behorighet for hogskolestudier" (basic Swedish higher-education entrance qualification) plus a bachelor's degree in music or equivalent completed by programme start. English/Swedish language requirements: UNVERIFIED.
acceptsNonMusic: NO as published - "a bachelor's degree in music or equivalent" by programme start. No clause addressing non-music degrees was found.
portfolioSpec: 3-4 portfolio pieces representing your creative work. At least ONE must be a QuickTime video (.mov) containing an original film score that you composed AND mixed. At least ONE must be sheet music in PDF; MP3 recordings must accompany any scores. Plus a one-page written statement of your study goals, and a CV documenting credentials and previous studies. Portfolio submission deadline was 21 January in the prior cycle (application deadline 15 January).
auditionSpec: Three-part process. Part 1: jury evaluation of the submitted works; those who pass advance. Part 2 - distance/take-home exam (due 23 February in the prior cycle): compose an independent theme, then write music to an assigned film clip incorporating that theme, submitting a lead sheet PDF, an MP3, a .mov video and a written rationale. Part 3 - INTERVIEW ON SITE at the Academy in week 10, discussing the submitted work, the exam tasks, your creative background and your expectations of the studies.
deadline: 15 January 2026 (application), portfolio 21 January 2026, distance exam 23 February 2026, on-site interview week 10 of 2026 - PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date
applicationOpens: UNVERIFIED (Swedish national cycle normally opens mid-October to 1 December)
tuitionIntl: Swedish non-EU/EEA tuition applies (Lund University fee-paying rules), but the amount for this specific programme is UNVERIFIED - request it from the Academy.
scholarship: None found - UNVERIFIED
fitNotes: The most transparently specified admission process in the Swedish slice, and the take-home scoring exam is exactly the kind of test a self-taught producer could actually smash - compose a theme, score a clip, mix it. But it is film/media scoring rather than club music, it demands a music bachelor and notated sheet music, and the final interview is on site in Malmo. Realistic only if he can produce notated scores; otherwise the sheet-music requirement alone disqualifies him.

program: Creative Music Technology - Master's programme (MMUST)
university: Norwegian University of Science and Technology (NTNU)
institutionType: Public university
durationEcts: 2 years / 120 ECTS, of which the thesis alone is 60 ECTS
focus: Electronic Music / Music technology and creative audio production
whatYouStudy: A practice-heavy degree: half the programme (60 ECTS) is the thesis itself, an artistic/creative project, with the remaining time in supporting courses. Focus on developing expertise in audio technology and its creative possibilities and on a "deeper aesthetic understanding of new musical expression made possible by technology", worked interdisciplinarily. An intensive introduction to AUDIO PROGRAMMING (Csound) is offered to those without prior experience - directly leverageable by a software engineer. Detailed course list beyond this: UNVERIFIED.
entryRequirements: "A bachelor's degree with a music technology specialization (at least 80 ECTS) or equivalent", with a grade point average of at least C. English proficiency required for all international students - IELTS, TOEFL or Pearson, and the test "should not be older than two years at time of the application deadline". Documents: passport, transcripts, diplomas, CV, motivation letter (max 1 page); non-EU/EEA applicants must also provide funding documentation.
acceptsNonMusic: CHECK - no on paper, but a real individual-assessment door exists. Published: "Admission requires an applicant to have completed a bachelor's degree with a music technology specialization (at least 80 ECTS) or equivalent. If you have a different background but think you are qualified, you will be able to apply and get an individual assessment of your previous qualifications." Only one external degree (Music Production from Kristiania University College) automatically qualifies; everything else, including his BSc, goes to individual assessment. Worth a direct pre-application enquiry with a portfolio attached.
portfolioSpec: NONE published on the admission page - required documents are passport, transcripts, diplomas, CV and a max 1-page motivation letter. Whether an artistic portfolio is requested during individual assessment: UNVERIFIED. Ask the programme coordinator.
auditionSpec: None published - no audition or on-site test listed.
tuitionIntl: NOK 198,800 per academic year (2025/2026) for students from outside the EU/EEA/Switzerland. Students admitted before autumn 2023 are exempt.
scholarship: "NTNU does not offer scholarships covering tuition costs." None found.
applicationOpens: UNVERIFIED (Norwegian non-EU cycle typically opens in October)
deadline: 1 December for non-EU/non-EEA applicants; 1 March for EU/EEA/Swiss; 15 April for Nordic citizens. PRIOR CYCLE pattern - for a September 2027 start expect 1 December 2026; confirm.
fitNotes: Very appealing structurally: English-taught, 60-ECTS creative thesis so he would spend a full year making work, no audition, no portfolio in the published requirements, and a Csound audio-programming on-ramp that rewards a software engineer. Two real problems: the 80-ECTS music-technology prerequisite means he must win an individual assessment, and NOK 198,800/yr with an explicit no-scholarship statement makes it the most expensive unfunded option in the slice. Note also that NTNU's separate Music, Communication and Technology (MCT) master no longer resolves on ntnu.edu (both its programme and admission pages return 404) - treat MCT as discontinued/UNVERIFIED.

program: Master of Music in Composition - specialisation Creative Music Technology
university: Norwegian Academy of Music (Norges musikkhogskole, NMH)
institutionType: Conservatory / state academy of music
durationEcts: 2 years / 120 ECTS, full-time, autumn start
focus: Electroacoustic Composition / Live Electronics / Sonic Arts with a strong technology component
whatYouStudy: The Composition master has four focus areas - acoustic composition, interdisciplinary composition, creative music technology and jazz composition. The Creative Music Technology specialisation is "aimed at composition students who wish to work with an expanded range of materials and approaches within an electroacoustic and music technology-oriented context" and "extends to include areas such as instrument design, electroacoustic composition, sound installation, video, electrical engineering, experimental performance practice, and creative programming". Delivery is seminar-based full-time study combining teacher-led instruction, academic supervision and independent study; attendance generally optional except where a course specifies otherwise. The core is a master project: an original artistic project with subprojects, developed from the first semester. One or two semesters abroad at partner institutions are possible without extending the degree. Staff include Anders Tveit (Assistant Professor, Music Technology) alongside composition professors Eivind Buene and Jon Henrik Hellstenius.
entryRequirements: Per the 2025 study plan: a Bachelor of Music with a minimum of 80 ECTS credits in Composition (jazz-composition applicants may substitute equivalent credits in jazz/improvised-music performance subjects or 80 credits in musicology). Entrance evaluation emphasises "original compositions" demonstrating a "high degree of artistic achievement". International applicants must additionally meet the GSU-list minimum academic qualifications (hkdir.no) and NMH's language requirements.
acceptsNonMusic: NO. The study plan requires "a Bachelor of Music with minimum 80 ECTS credits in Composition". A BSc Software Engineering does not qualify and no discretionary clause was found on the pages read.
portfolioSpec: Original compositions are submitted for jury evaluation, with assessment weighted on "original compositions" showing high artistic achievement - but the exact number of works, durations, formats and accompanying documents are NOT published on the pages read. UNVERIFIED - request the audition requirements from opptak@nmh.no.
auditionSpec: UNVERIFIED - the admission pages read do not state whether a live audition/interview is required or whether recorded submissions suffice for overseas applicants. Confirm with opptak@nmh.no.
tuitionIntl: NOK 220,000 per academic year for students from outside the EU/EEA/Switzerland (performance studies at NMH). Must be paid IN FULL by 1 June before the academic year starts - instalments are not permitted, and missing the deadline means automatic loss of study rights. Exempt: exchange students from NMH partner universities, and students who began before autumn 2023.
scholarship: "NMH does not provide financial aid to cover tuition costs." None found.

deadline: 15 December for undergraduate and graduate programmes (applications open 1 November). PRIOR CYCLE pattern - for a September 2027 start expect 15 December 2026; confirm.
fitNotes: Excellent facilities and a genuinely technology-forward composition environment (instrument design, sound installation, creative programming) in Norway's leading music academy. For this candidate it is effectively closed: the 80-ECTS-in-composition prerequisite is the strictest gate in the slice, tuition is NOK 220,000/yr payable in one lump by 1 June with zero scholarships, and the portfolio spec is not even published. Note also that NMH's former "Master of Music in Performance Technology and Electroacoustic Composition" no longer appears among current graduate programmes - it has been absorbed into this Composition master.

program: Master's Programme in Popular Music - specialisation Electronic Music
university: University of Agder (UiA)
institutionType: Public university

language: English (taught in English at the Kristiansand campus)

whatYouStudy: The programme emphasises balancing "practice, composition, programming and production" with theoretical grounding in popular musicology. The Electronic Music specialisation focuses on "music technology and sound design in the studio, or use of Live Electronics in a concert context" and on "performance and its relationship to music technology and sound design". Sibling specialisations: Performing Music, World Music, Songwriting, and Music Business and Management. UiA also runs a Bachelor in Electronic Music, so the department has an established electronic-music teaching base.
entryRequirements: A bachelor's degree or equivalent of at least three years (180 credits) with at least 20 credits at level 2 in the specialisation unit; for the Electronic Music/performance specialisations, at least 80 credits in performing music / electronic music, a music-technology degree, or another approved programme; minimum grade average of C across the bachelor. Performance specialisations also require "a very high level on the principle instrument" plus documented music theory/analysis coursework equivalent to UiA's own bachelor. Programme coordinator: Per Elias Drablos (per.e.drablos@uia.no).
acceptsNonMusic: NO as published - the entry route requires "at least 80 credits in performing/electronic music, music technology degree, or other approved programs" plus a C average, plus documented music theory/analysis. A pure software-engineering BSc would need an exceptional individual assessment; nothing on the pages read promises one.
portfolioSpec: Applicants submit a PROJECT PROPOSAL with the application, which feeds the evaluation. The exact audio/video portfolio specification (number of works, durations, formats) is NOT published on the pages read - UNVERIFIED. Request it from the programme coordinator.
auditionSpec: Entrance exam has two equally weighted parts: AUDITION worth 50% of the score with a minimum of 10 out of 20 required to pass, and INTERVIEW worth 50% (also scored 10-20), held only after the audition is passed. Whether the audition may be submitted as a recording or held online for overseas applicants: UNVERIFIED - confirm before booking travel.
tuitionIntl: NOK 135,000 per academic year (60 ECTS) for 2026/2027 - Category B, which explicitly covers the Master in Popular Music and the Master in Popular Music - Music Business and Management. Payment deadline 1 September for active students. The cheapest Norwegian option in this slice.
scholarship: "The University of Agder does not offer any scholarships for 2026/2027." None found; no fee waivers mentioned.
applicationOpens: 1 November
deadline: Non-EU/EEA international applicants: 1 November - 15 December, with an extended deadline of 15 April 2026 noted for the 2026 intake - PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date; expect 1 Nov - 15 Dec 2026 for a Sept 2027 start
fitNotes: Of all the Nordic craft-focused options this is the closest fit to "I want to make electronic music and perform it": English-taught, an explicit Electronic Music specialisation covering studio sound design and live electronics, entrepreneurship and audience-development modules that map onto a DJ career, and at NOK 135,000/yr it is roughly a third the cost of NTNU or NMH. The obstacles are the 80-credits-in-music prerequisite, an audition worth 50% of the score whose remote-submission status is unpublished, and a flat no-scholarship policy. Highest-value action in this slice: email Per Elias Drablos in autumn 2026 with a portfolio and ask directly whether an engineering BSc plus documented electronic-music practice can satisfy the 80-credit rule.

program: Master's Programme in Music Technology - study profiles: Recording Arts / Film and Game Music Producer / Creative Electronic Music Practices

institutionType: Conservatory / national university of the arts

language: Finnish, Swedish and English - and "English having a very pronounced status within the Music Technology programme"
focus: Recording / Engineering + Film & Game Sound + Electronic Music Production (choose one of three profiles)
whatYouStudy: You select ONE of three study profiles at application: Recording Arts; Film and Game Music Producer; or Creative Electronic Music Practices. The Music Technology department also shares teaching with Aalto's Media Lab (Aalto students may take Sibelius Academy Music Technology courses, and vice versa). entryRequirements: Eligibility routes: a lower university degree in music; OR "a lower university degree in another field and, additionally, higher education studies in music"; OR an applicable foreign degree that provides eligibility for corresponding higher-education studies in the awarding country. Non-EU applicants pay a EUR 100 application fee.
acceptsNonMusic: THE CLOSEST TO A YES IN THIS SLICE, with one condition. Published wording: eligibility via "a lower university degree in another field and, additionally, higher education studies in music", and applicants holding "a higher education degree in the field of technology or media" may apply if they have sufficient music coursework. A BSc Software Engineering is therefore explicitly contemplated as a base degree - but he must first acquire DOCUMENTED higher-education music studies (e.g. open-university music courses, a music-technology certificate) to bolt onto it. That is a concrete, achievable action item before the 2027 call opens.
portfolioSpec: ADVANCE ASSIGNMENTS = 40% of the total evaluation. (1) Portfolio and presentation: MAXIMUM 10 MINUTES TOTAL, with a 3-minute presentation recommended; include UP TO 3 WORKS, at least one of which must be audio or audiovisual; formats MP3 for audio or MP4 with H.264/AAC codecs for video. (2) Project description form as PDF detailing each portfolio work. (3) Motivation letter, maximum 2 A4 pages. (4) CV covering education, training, artistic work and experience. (5) Final project plan, maximum 2 A4 pages. (6) Study plan of maximum 150 ECTS.
auditionSpec: ENTRANCE EXAMINATION = 60% of the total evaluation, held REMOTELY (prior cycle: 31 March - 1 April). Two components: an INSTRUMENT/VOICE AUDITION of 7-10 minutes worth 40% of the exam, demonstrating technical proficiency and musical sensitivity; and an INTERVIEW of up to 25 minutes worth 60% of the exam, covering your portfolio, your performance, your background and the feasibility of your project. Note the instrument/voice audition is a real hurdle for a non-instrumentalist - clarify with siba.admissions@uniarts.fi how it is applied to Music Technology applicants.
tuitionIntl: EUR 28,000 per academic year for non-EU/EEA/Swiss students in English-taught programmes starting August 2026 or later. "The amount of the fee will stay the same for the statutory duration of your degree studies." Plus a EUR 100 application fee. The single most expensive option in this slice.
scholarship: Explicitly none from the university: "The university does not grant any scholarships to cover the tuition fee for students starting in August 2026 or later", and "Uniarts Helsinki does not grant scholarships for living expenses." ONE published workaround: Finnish- and Swedish-taught programmes are exempt from fees, and "students may apply to change their language of study to Finnish or Swedish", eliminating the fee going forward - relevant here because Music Technology's languages of tuition include Finnish and Swedish. Whether the national Finland Scholarship (EUR 5,000 relocation grant, first year of master's studies) applies at Uniarts: UNVERIFIED.
fundingLevel: None from the institution (unless the Finnish/Swedish language-of-study route is available and workable)

deadline: 21 January 2026 at 15:00 EET (supporting documents by 28 January 2026, 15:00 EET); entrance exams 31 March - 1 April 2026 remotely; results 10 April 2026; study-place confirmation by 9 July 2026 - PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date from the admissions guide published Oct-Nov 2026

Two serious obstacles: EUR 28,000/yr with a written no-scholarship policy makes it self-pay-only unless the Finnish/Swedish language-of-study exemption can be used, and there is a 7-10 minute instrument/voice audition worth 40% of the entrance exam. Action items before the Oct-Nov 2026 guide drops: acquire documented higher-education music studies, and email siba.admissions@uniarts.fi about both the instrument audition and the Finnish/Swedish fee-exemption route.

whatYouStudy: The programme combines the art, design and media-driven aspects of sound, "covering a wide range of disciplines from concept design to live performance and from storytelling to programming". Study areas: sound design, sonic interaction, music technology, audio-visual production and interactive art. acceptsNonMusic: YES in practice - the only stated degree requirement is a "relevant Bachelor's degree" with NO music-degree and NO music-theory requirement, and this is a design/technology programme run by Aalto Media Lab whose remit explicitly spans programming and concept design. auditionSpec: Two-phase selection, NO live on-site audition. Phase I evaluates motivation and background. Phase II comprises portfolio review, assignments (written or AUDIO-BASED), and a 30-minute interview.
tuitionIntl: EUR 20,000 per academic year for non-EU/EEA/Swiss citizens. EU/EEA and Swiss citizens pay nothing.
scholarship: Aalto University Scholarship: covers EITHER 50% OR 100% of the tuition fee for the standard duration of the degree (two years full-time for a master's). fundingLevel: Full or partial (competitive tuition waiver of 50% or 100%)
stipend: Tuition waiver only (50% or 100%); no living-cost stipend published
applicationOpens: 1 December (opened 1 Dec 2025 for the 2026 intake)

Treat as the primary Nordic application, with the Aalto and Sibelius Academy applications prepared together since they share a portfolio.

program: Reżyseria dźwięku (Sound Engineering / Sound Direction), studia II stopnia — specialisations: reżyseria muzyczna, reżyseria dźwięku w filmie i telewizji, reżyseria dźwięku w multimediach

Students may extend the programme with additional multimedia subjects.

Czech-language study means a Czech certificate at B2/C1 (CCE) is in practice required to enrol and to keep tuition-free status. Full-time attendance only — no distance form. IELTS/TOEFL is irrelevant here; Czech is the gate.
portfolioSpec: Round 1 (documents only, candidate not present): (1) a LIST of all own sound works made during bachelor's study — audiovisual/multimedia works, music recordings, radio and theatre sound design — each with title, genre, director, production company, duration, year; (2) TWO audiovisual works on which the applicant made a substantial sound contribution, each with a detailed written explication; (3) the applicant's own theoretical work or an essay in the field; (4) a written project/statement for the master's study at FAMU (intended specialisation, expected outcomes, elective courses wanted at FAMU or other universities, interest in international internships). All works must be the applicant's own authorship, confirmed by a signed declaration. Works are uploaded by the separate works deadline (1 Sept in the 2026/27 cycle), not with the application form.
auditionSpec: Round 2 is an IN-PERSON oral examination in Prague: interview testing technical and artistic knowledge of the field, musical competence, and readiness for master's-level work, plus defence of the submitted works and the study project.
acceptsNonMusic: Check — formally yes, practically hard. The department page states candidates from other schools and fields may apply with any bachelor's degree, but adds they should show theoretical and practical knowledge equivalent to graduates of the programme's own bachelor track. There is no wording excluding a software-engineering BSc, but the portfolio (two finished audiovisual works with sound by the applicant) is the real filter.
deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. 2026/27 cycle (from the official specific-conditions PDF): applications 1 June – 13 August 2026; works/portfolio upload by 1 September 2026; Round 1 on 14 September 2026; Round 2 on 17 September 2026. NOTE the unusual summer cycle — for a September 2027 start expect an analogous June–August 2027 window, i.e. much later than most European deadlines.
applicationOpens: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. 1 June (2026 cycle opened 1 June 2026 via prihlaska.amu.cz). Application fee 990 CZK.
tuitionIntl: 0 CZK for study in Czech at a Czech public university — nationality is irrelevant under Czech law; only study in a foreign language is charged. (For comparison, FAMU's English-taught MFA programmes cost CZK 550,000 per year in 2026/27 — but none of those is Sound Design.)
scholarship: No dedicated scholarship found for Tunisians. Czech Government Scholarships (Developing Countries) do NOT cover Tunisia — the 2026/27 eligible list was Bosnia & Herzegovina, Georgia, Ukraine, Belarus (democratic forces), Guatemala and Jordan. AMU offers internal accommodation, social and merit scholarships (eligibility for non-EU students UNVERIFIED).
fundingLevel: Partial (tuition-free if studying in Czech; living costs self-funded)
stipend: Tuition waiver by law (Czech-taught). No stipend identified. UNVERIFIED whether AMU internal scholarships reach non-EU first-year master's students.
facilities: FAMU's Department of Sound (Katedra zvukové tvorby, Smetanovo nábřeží 2, Prague 1) runs mixing and post-production rooms integrated with the school's film production pipeline; the department describes 'a combination of technologies allowing students to finish films in first-class quality' and active collaboration with the Czech film industry for placements and contacts. Audio-recording teaching is partly delivered by HAMU's Sound Studio. Exact Dolby Atmos certification of FAMU rooms: UNVERIFIED. FAMU alumni include Miloš Forman, Věra Chytilová, Jiří Menzel, Emir Kusturica, Agnieszka Holland.
fitNotes: The most prestigious name on this slice and genuinely hands-on, but it is a FILM sound school, not a music-production school — nothing here trains him as a DJ or a club/electronic producer. Two obstacles compound: Czech at B2/C1 for the free route, and a portfolio of two finished audiovisual works with his own sound design, which he does not have. Realistic only as a 2028+ target after building a film/game sound reel; the June–August application window at least gives him a full extra year of preparation.

program: Zvuková tvorba a hudební režie — specializace Zvuková tvorba (Sound Design / recording engineering), navazující magisterské studium
university: Akademie múzických umění v Praze — HAMU (Music and Dance Faculty)
institutionType: Public conservatory / academy of music (music faculty of AMU)
focus: Recording/Engineering; Music Production; Electronic Music/Live Electronics; Immersive Audio
durationEcts: 2 years; ECTS total UNVERIFIED (standard Czech follow-up master = 120 ECTS)
whatYouStudy: Artistic-technical sound work at the highest level of autonomous sound creation: classical-music and jazz recording technique, realisation of electroacoustic music, sound and music post-production, live sound reinforcement, concert recording, online streaming, and sound-to-picture. Taught content covers microphone technique, signal processing, spatial/dynamic/timbral transformation of sound, analogue and digital console practice, and research methodology in musical and psychological acoustics. Graduates work as recording engineers in professional music studios, radio sound engineers, and in-house engineers for cultural institutions.
entryRequirements: Bachelor's degree. Applicants must submit a CURRENT AUDIOGRAM with an ENT specialist's statement — a hearing test is a formal admission condition. Czech-language study; Czech at B2/C1 needed in practice.
portfolioSpec: 'Presentation of audio recordings' by the candidate, presented and defended in Round 2. The department does NOT publish a number of works, a maximum duration or a file format on its admissions page — UNVERIFIED beyond 'presentation of own recordings'; contact katedra zvukové tvorby a hudební režie for the exact spec.
auditionSpec: Yes — two IN-PERSON rounds in Prague. Round 1: electronic/aural test (analysis of a sound signal, stereo imaging, melodic and rhythmic patterns, detection of sound faults) plus a written knowledge test in physiological, spatial and musical acoustics, musical electronics and sound engineering; minimum 20 of 25 points to progress. Round 2: practical mix of speech + music + noise on an ANALOGUE console (~2 min); mix of abstract electronic music on a DIGITAL console (max ~2 min); a basic instrumental proficiency test (piano preferred); presentation of own recordings; interview on professional vision.
acceptsNonMusic: Yes, conditionally — quoted from the programme page: students coming from other bachelor's programmes may enrol 'if they meet minimum technical and artistic requirements for the Sound Creation specialisation', and will progressively make up missing bachelor-level knowledge through elective courses. The hard filter is not the diploma but the Round-1 hearing/acoustics test and the piano/instrument test.
deadline: UNVERIFIED — the department page points to its 'Magisterské studium' section for current dates and does not publish them inline. Confirm directly for the 2027/28 cycle.
applicationOpens: UNVERIFIED. Application fee 990 CZK, paid by card via prihlaska.amu.cz.
tuitionIntl: 0 CZK for Czech-taught study at a Czech public university, any nationality.
scholarship: None found specific to Tunisians (Czech Government Scholarships exclude Tunisia). AMU internal accommodation/social/merit scholarships exist; eligibility for non-EU students UNVERIFIED.
fundingLevel: Partial (tuition-free in Czech; living costs self-funded)
facilities: HAMU's own Zvukové studio (Sound Studio) at Malostranské náměstí 258/13, Prague 1 — analogue and digital mixing consoles, recording studio used for classical/jazz sessions, and the facility that also delivers audio-recording teaching to FAMU. Department also runs bachelor, master and doctoral levels plus faculty-wide electives.
fitNotes: This is the closest thing in Prague to a Tonmeister/recording-engineering master, and its electroacoustic and post-production strands touch electronic music. But the entrance exam is brutal for a self-taught producer: an acoustics knowledge test, an ear/fault-detection test with a 20/25 pass bar, a live analogue-console mix, and a piano test — plus a medical audiogram. Czech is required. Not realistic for September 2027 without a year of Czech plus serious classical-recording and keyboard preparation.

program: Zvuková tvorba a hudební režie — specializace Hudební režie (Music Direction / classical record production), navazující magisterské studium
university: Akademie múzických umění v Praze — HAMU
institutionType: Public academy of music
focus: Recording/Engineering; Music Production (classical record production)
durationEcts: 2 years; ECTS UNVERIFIED
whatYouStudy: Training as a classical music producer/record producer: leading complex orchestral and chamber recording sessions, detailed score analysis and instrumental knowledge, session planning and direction, post-production (editing, mixing) in professional DAWs, live concert recording with streaming integration, audiovisual projects, and communication/team leadership with artists and the recording crew.
entryRequirements: Bachelor's degree plus very high musical literacy — score reading, orchestration knowledge, aural dictation and piano are all examined. Czech-language study.
portfolioSpec: Presentation of own sound recordings in Round 2. Exact number/duration/format not published — UNVERIFIED.
auditionSpec: Yes — IN-PERSON, two rounds. Round 1: written practical + theoretical test, ear-training dictation and listening comprehension, score analysis and orchestration assessment, and a piano proficiency examination. Round 2: presentation of sound recordings and an interview on artistic vision and professional orientation.
acceptsNonMusic: No in practice. The page states no formal bar on the prior degree, but Round 1 examines score analysis, orchestration, aural dictation and piano — a software-engineering BSc holder without conservatory training cannot pass. Treat as effectively closed.
deadline: UNVERIFIED — check the department's Magisterské studium page for the 2027/28 cycle.

tuitionIntl: 0 CZK (Czech-taught, public university).
scholarship: None found for Tunisians.
facilities: HAMU Sound Studio, Malostranské nám. 258/13, Prague 1; access to orchestral and chamber ensembles of the academy for recording sessions. Guarantor doc. Ing. MgA. Ondřej Urban, Ph.D.
fitNotes: Listed for completeness as the region's classical record-production master. It is a genuine craft degree, but it is aimed at conservatory-trained musicians and is the wrong instrument entirely for a DJ/electronic-producer ambition. Recommend skipping.

program: Zvukový design a multimediální technologie (Sound Design and Multimedia Technologies) — navazující magisterské studium
university: Masarykova univerzita (Masaryk University), Faculty of Arts — Department of Musicology, jointly delivered with FEKT VUT Brno
institutionType: Public university (Faculty of Arts), taught jointly with the Brno University of Technology electrical-engineering faculty and industry practitioners
focus: Sound Design; Music Production; Recording/Engineering; Immersive Audio
durationEcts: 2 years / 120 ECTS; full-time (prezenční) or part-time (kombinovaná)
whatYouStudy: Four strands over four semesters: (1) technical foundations — mathematics, physics, acoustics, studio technology; (2) production foundations — sound design proper; (3) sound production and programming — recording-studio work, audio software, autonomous sound production in the digital environment, live music production sound; (4) theory, history and contemporary practice of sound creation. Practical skills training runs through all four semesters and a MANDATORY external internship is part of the degree. Taught by leading practitioners alongside MUNI musicologists and BUT engineers.
entryRequirements: Any bachelor's degree. Quoted from the official page: 'Program je určen absolventům bakalářského studia – bez omezení' (the programme is intended for bachelor's graduates — without restriction). Czech-language study, so Czech at B2/C1 is the practical requirement.
portfolioSpec: No conventional portfolio of finished works is demanded. Instead the second exam component is a CREATIVE PROJECT PROPOSAL of maximum 2 pages, setting out motivation and the intended creative/research direction. (Own works can be referenced in support but are not a stated fixed requirement.)
auditionSpec: Oral entrance examination in two parts: (a) professional and artistic competence — technical, production and theoretical knowledge; (b) discussion of the max-2-page creative project. Scoring: pass mark 50 of 100; the professional exam is worth 40 points and the creative project 60 points. On-site oral exam in Brno.
acceptsNonMusic: YES — explicitly. 'Program je určen absolventům bakalářského studia – bez omezení' ('for bachelor graduates — without restriction'). This is the only programme found in the whole Czech/Slovak/Hungarian slice that states openness to any bachelor field in writing, which makes a software-engineering BSc formally unproblematic.
deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. 2026 cycle: applications 1 January – 30 April 2026, with the entrance exam after. For a September 2027 start expect 1 January – 30 April 2027.
applicationOpens: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. 1 January (2026 cycle opened 1 January 2026).
tuitionIntl: 0 CZK for Czech-taught study at a Czech public university, regardless of nationality. Non-EU applicants pay only the standard application fee. Exact MUNI application fee for this programme: UNVERIFIED.
scholarship: None found earmarked for Tunisians; Czech Government Scholarships do not cover Tunisia. MUNI runs internal merit and social scholarships — eligibility for non-EU master's students UNVERIFIED.
stipend: Tuition waiver only; no stipend identified. UNVERIFIED.
facilities: Recording-studio work and live-sound practice built into the curriculum; technical teaching and laboratories supplied by FEKT VUT Brno (anechoic chamber, audio labs); compulsory external internship places students in Czech industry. Detailed equipment list UNVERIFIED.
fitNotes: The single best structural fit in Czechia for a software-engineering graduate: it explicitly accepts any bachelor, its entrance test is a knowledge interview plus a two-page project rather than a portfolio of finished films, its engineering half rewards a technical background, and its production half (studio recording, live sound, digital production) is close to what he actually wants. The one real obstacle is Czech at B2/C1 — which would need a year of intensive Czech before applying in January 2027. Worth building the whole Czech plan around.

program: Teorie a praxe audiovizuální tvorby — specializace Zvuková skladba (Sound Composition), navazující magisterské studium
university: Univerzita Tomáše Bati ve Zlíně (Tomas Bata University), Faculty of Multimedia Communications (FMK)
institutionType: Public university, multimedia/film faculty (Zlín is the historic centre of Czech film production)
focus: Film/Game Sound; Sound Design; Music Production
language: Czech (the faculty states Czech readiness is verified through the entrance examination itself)
durationEcts: 2 years, full-time; ECTS UNVERIFIED (standard 120)
whatYouStudy: Theory and practice of sound composition with an explicit emphasis on SOUND DRAMATURGY in audiovisual work. Coursework named on the official page: sound composition for audiovisual media, production practicum, television formats, live broadcast operations, music history, theory of visual culture, contemporary film analysis. Graduates go into film, broadcasting, theatre, music production and advertising as sound engineers/sound designers.
entryRequirements: Bachelor's degree; applicants to design and multimedia programmes at FMK submit work samples with the application. Czech-language study.
portfolioSpec: Work samples (práce) submitted with the application for design/multimedia programmes — the exact count, duration and format for the Zvuková skladba specialisation are NOT published on the pages read. UNVERIFIED; request the specialisation's 'požadavky k přijímací zkoušce' from studium@fmk.utb.cz.
auditionSpec: On-site entrance examination in Zlín — one exam date for the whole Teorie a praxe audiovizuální tvorby programme (10 June 2026 in the prior cycle). Format details UNVERIFIED.
acceptsNonMusic: Check — no wording found either permitting or excluding a non-audiovisual bachelor. The programme is a follow-up master in audiovisual creation and the work-sample requirement implies prior practical output. Confirm with the faculty.
deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. 2026 cycle: applications 1 January – 30 April 2026; entrance exam 10 June 2026; admission decisions by 7 July 2026; enrolment July 2026. For September 2027 entry expect January–April 2027.
applicationOpens: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. 1 January (via eprihlaska.utb.cz). Administrative fee 990 CZK.
tuitionIntl: 0 CZK for Czech-taught study at a public university, any nationality.
scholarship: None found for Tunisians. UTB internal scholarships UNVERIFIED.
facilities: FMK is built on the Zlín film-studio tradition and runs an Ateliér audiovizuální tvorby with film production facilities; specific sound rooms/console/Atmos equipment UNVERIFIED.

Same two blockers: Czech, and a work sample he cannot yet produce. Sound dramaturgy for film, not club music — so it serves the sound-design half of his ambition, not the DJ half.

program: Audio inženýrství (Audio Engineering) — navazující magisterský program, specializace Zvuková produkce a nahrávání (Sound Production and Recording)
university: Vysoké učení technické v Brně (Brno University of Technology), Faculty of Electrical Engineering and Communication (FEKT), Department of Telecommunications — artistic subjects delivered by JAMU Music Faculty
institutionType: Public technical university, in formal cooperation with the Janáček Academy of Performing Arts (JAMU)
focus: Recording/Engineering; Music Production; Immersive Audio
durationEcts: 2 years / minimum 120 ECTS. The Zvuková produkce a nahrávání specialisation requires 72 credits of compulsory courses, at least 37 credits from elective-compulsory groups and at least 6 free-elective credits.
whatYouStudy: Two specialisations exist: 'Zvuková produkce a nahrávání' (Sound Production and Recording — the music/production one) and 'Akustika a audiovizuální technika' (Acoustics and AV Technology). The production track covers recording technique for different instruments and building the mix, studio practice, audio effects design, compression algorithms, hardware and software implementation of audio processing, sound analysis, multimedia/interactive/VR audio, plus room acoustics. The JAMU partnership lets students take filmmaking and multimedia-composition subjects with JAMU staff. Anechoic chamber and sound laboratory measurement work are part of the course.
entryRequirements: A bachelor's degree with 'appropriate electrical engineering qualifications' per the programme record — i.e. a technical/engineering background is expected. Czech-language study. Accreditation runs 1 May 2018 – 1 May 2028.
portfolioSpec: None stated — this is a technical master with a knowledge-based admission, not a portfolio admission. Exact entrance-exam waiver/eligibility rules for holders of a non-Czech, non-electrical bachelor: UNVERIFIED.
auditionSpec: None. No live audition or artistic test found; admission is on prior degree/academic record with a possible knowledge examination. Details UNVERIFIED.
acceptsNonMusic: Yes for the non-music point — a music degree is explicitly NOT needed; this is the one programme in the slice where a technical bachelor is the expected input. The stated condition is instead 'appropriate electrical engineering qualifications', so a software-engineering BSc must be checked against the required signal-processing/electronics coursework. Quote from the programme record: students must possess 'appropriate electrical engineering qualifications' to enter.
deadline: UNVERIFIED for the 2027/28 cycle. VUT master's applications typically close around the end of April — confirm on vut.cz.
applicationOpens: UNVERIFIED.
tuitionIntl: 0 CZK for Czech-taught study at a Czech public university, any nationality. VUT's English-taught programmes are fee-paying; Audio inženýrství is recorded as Czech-language only.
scholarship: None found for Tunisians. VUT merit scholarships exist; non-EU eligibility UNVERIFIED.
facilities: FEKT sound laboratory and anechoic chamber; studio recording practice; JAMU's professional recording studio, two electroacoustic music studios, modular synthesiser, multichannel systems and field-recording equipment are accessible through the cooperation. Programme guarantor doc. Ing. Jiří Schimmel, Ph.D. Reported 97% employment within three months of graduating (figure published by FEKT for the linked bachelor track).
fitNotes: The best 'leverage your CS degree' option in the region — DSP, audio software, plugin/effect design and studio recording in one degree, with JAMU artistic subjects bolted on. It makes him an audio engineer/audio developer rather than a DJ, but it is the one route where his existing background is an asset instead of an obstacle. Blockers: Czech-language instruction, and confirming that a Tunisian software-engineering BSc satisfies the 'electrical engineering qualifications' clause.

program: Multimediální tvorba (Multimedia Creation) — navazující magisterské studium
university: Janáčkova akademie múzických umění v Brně (JAMU), Faculty of Music — Department of Composition and Multimedia Creation
institutionType: Public academy of performing arts (music faculty)
focus: Electronic Music/Live Electronics; Sonic Arts; Sound Design

whatYouStudy: Taught since 2008 (originally as 'Multimedia Composition'). Students work across performance, happening, sonic objects, interactive installations, net art, interactive video projection, opera, dance, video clips, experimental documentary and computer games. Teaching is shared across four institutions — JAMU's Music and Theatre faculties, the Faculty of Fine Arts at BUT, and Masaryk University's Faculty of Arts. Graduates become authors of musical, audio or multimedia works, multimedia specialists, or new-media dramaturges for theatres, arts agencies and multimedia festivals.

Dan Dlouhý, dlouhy@jamu.cz) where candidates can discuss admission requirements before applying — a genuinely useful door for an unconventional applicant.

Expect a portfolio of own multimedia/sound works plus a talent examination; confirm the exact spec with the department.

acceptsNonMusic: Check — not stated for this specialisation. Note that the sister specialisation (Kompozice elektroakustické hudby) explicitly admits bachelor graduates from other institutions via entrance and placement exams, which suggests the department is used to non-standard entrants. Confirm via the talent advisory service.
deadline: UNVERIFIED for 2027/28 — check hf.jamu.cz/uchazeci-hf/prijimaci-rizeni/.
applicationOpens: UNVERIFIED.

Czech is required and the portfolio spec is unpublished, so the practical first step is an email to the talent advisory service. Worth a direct enquiry.

program: Kompozice — specializace Kompozice elektroakustické hudby (Electroacoustic Music Composition)

program: Strihová a zvuková skladba — študijný plán Zvuková skladba (Sound Composition / Sound Design), magisterské štúdium
university: Vysoká škola múzických umení v Bratislave (VŠMU / Academy of Performing Arts), Film and Television Faculty (FTF) — Ateliér zvukovej skladby
institutionType: Public film and television faculty of a national academy of performing arts
focus: Film/Game Sound; Sound Design; Immersive Audio; Recording/Engineering
durationEcts: 2 years (4 semesters) / 120 ECTS, full-time (denná forma)
whatYouStudy: Named courses on the official page: Mixing and Mastering; Sound Creation – Audiovisual Production; Film Sound Theory; Music Recording Theory and Practice; Sound Design Theory – Musical Dramaturgy; Music Direction; Sound Synthesis. Theory and practice are oriented to SURROUND formats, and the master level explicitly targets film sound in Dolby Surround 7.1 and Dolby Atmos, plus film music. The stated aim is independent creative thinking in sound composition for audiovisual work of any genre — training 'sound masters' who use sound expressive means to realise a dramaturgical intent.
entryRequirements: Completed bachelor's degree before enrolment. Slovak-language instruction. Electronic application via ePrihláška; application fee €40.
portfolioSpec: UNVERIFIED at the level of exact specification — the atelier page states requirements and exam procedures are published per programme page, and the programme page gives dates and fee but not the portfolio spec. Expect submitted sound works with explications; request the 'požiadavky na prijímacie skúšky' from the study coordinator Jana Mihoková (jana.mihokova@vsmu.sk, +421 2 2100 6511 ext. 511).

Note that the Music and Dance Faculty of the same university runs a two-round process with an online interview for international applicants — whether FTF offers any remote option is UNVERIFIED and worth asking.
acceptsNonMusic: Check — no statement found on the programme page about the required field of the prior bachelor. Ask the coordinator directly; the atelier trains sound engineers and sound designers rather than musicians, so the question is genuinely open.
deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. 2026 cycle for Zvuková skladba Mgr. art.: application deadline 8 April 2026; entrance exam 23 June 2026. For September 2027 entry expect roughly April 2027 with a June 2027 exam.
applicationOpens: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. Via ePrihláška; opening date UNVERIFIED, fee €40.

(By contrast the Music and Dance Faculty's English-language track is €5,000/year — that is a different faculty and not this programme.)

Reported at up to €1,025 per month, up to €10,000 total over two academic years, with roughly 45 master's places globally. Tuition is not automatically covered but Slovak-taught full-time study is already free.
fundingLevel: Full (potentially) — tuition-free by default plus a monthly stipend if the SAIA scholarship is won; otherwise Partial (tuition-free only).
stipend: Up to €1,025/month for up to 2 academic years (~€10,000 total) under the Slovak scholarship for talented foreign students. Amounts as reported — confirm on studyinslovakia.saia.sk and scholarships.portalvs.sk. PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date: the 2026/27 round closed 31 July 2026, so expect a ~July 2027 deadline for 2027/28.
facilities: Founded 1999. Described on the official page as one of Slovakia's most modern audio complexes and holding DOLBY ATMOS MUSIC STUDIO certification: five sound mixing suites, a cinema hall, professional microphones and field-recording equipment, working from stereo through multichannel for cinema and streaming. A development project upgrades one mixing suite to Dolby Atmos 12.1 and the cinema to Dolby Atmos 39.2, positioning the atelier as a teaching centre for 3D spatial audio. Head: Mgr. art. Tobiáš Potočný, ArtD.; staff include prof. Peter Mojžiš, doc. Dušan Kozák, doc. Marek Piaček.
fitNotes: Best combination in this slice of world-class facilities (Dolby Atmos Music certified, five mixing suites), zero tuition for everyone, and a real chance of a €1,025/month government stipend — the only plausibly FULLY FUNDED route across Czechia, Slovakia and Hungary for this profile. The blocker is Slovak-language instruction, which is a serious commitment with no Arabic/French bridge, plus an unpublished portfolio spec and an on-site June exam. Also note it is film/TV sound and immersive audio, not DJ/club production.

program: Zeneszerző MA (Music Composition MA) — Elektronikus zenei médiaművészet (Electronic Music Media Art / EZMM) specialisation

institutionType: Public conservatory / national academy of music
focus: Electroacoustic Composition; Electronic Music/Live Electronics; Sonic Arts

durationEcts: 2 years (4 semesters); ECTS UNVERIFIED (Hungarian MA standard 120)
whatYouStudy: Composition at master level with the option to deepen electronic-music work; the EZMM strand continues the Academy's electronic music media art line (launched 2011) covering the history and compositional technique of electroacoustic and computer music, sound analysis, synthesis and transformation, MIDI/OSC, interactive and algorithmic music. Composition-related special courses are chosen freely according to the student's interests. Applicants who did NOT take electronic-music courses in their prior studies must complete a 2-semester 'Foundations of Electronic Music Composition' course during the first MA year.
entryRequirements: BA diploma. All applicants must submit a PRELIMINARY CREDIT RECOGNITION REQUEST to establish whether their BA diploma can be accepted for the MA, unless the BA was taken at the Liszt Academy — the request form plus the BA transcript/diploma supplement and English course descriptions go in with the application. Certificates need an official certified attested Hungarian translation. Applications route through felvi.hu (Hungarian central admissions) or through the Stipendium Hungaricum portal.
portfolioSpec: Uploaded portfolio evaluated first: sheet music of THREE of the applicant's own compositions, with recordings if possible. For the EZMM specialisation the presented works must total NO MORE THAN 25–30 MINUTES and comprise (a) one recorded tape/fixed-media piece and (b) one work for instrument + electronics, OR an interactive live performance, OR an audiovisual work. Style exercises additionally required: one fugue in the style of J. S. Bach (EZMM candidates may realise the Bach-style task electroacoustically), one classical sonata or rondo movement, and one 20th-century etude in the style of a named composer. EZMM candidates also sit an electronic-music fundamentals test.
auditionSpec: YES — mandatory in-person. 'All applicants are required to appear before the Entrance Examination Committee in person.' Components: a practical examination (live audition) in the chosen specialisation; a written theoretical examination; written and oral form analysis based on Schoenberg's 'Fundamentals of Musical Composition' including analysis of classical/romantic and 20th–21st century works; an on-site orchestration/scoring task; score reading (sight-reading classical/romantic and contemporary scores); and a career-orientation interview.
acceptsNonMusic: No, in practice. Nothing formally bars a non-music BA, but the mandatory preliminary credit-recognition check on the BA diploma, plus a Bach fugue, a classical sonata/rondo movement, score sight-reading and an orchestration task, make a software-engineering BSc holder without conservatory theory effectively unadmittable. Quote from the Academy: applicants 'must submit a preliminary credit recognition request to determine whether the applicant's BA diploma can be accepted to apply for the MA programme'.

applicationOpens: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. Stipendium Hungaricum 2027/28 reported to open November 2026.

program: Biennio Accademico di II livello in Music Production (Diploma Accademico di Secondo Livello in Music Production)
