whatYouStudy: Verified from the official page. Each student learns to run a music-production project through every phase, from the creative idea to arrangement with real and virtual instruments, recording, mixing and mastering. Named modules: LABORATORIO DI PRODUZIONE — developing original projects with a music-producer's approach to the whole production chain; TECNICHE DI RIPRESA E REGISTRAZIONE — each specialising student produces TWO TRACKS end-to-end, from pre-production and arrangement through rehearsals, recording and overdubbing, microphone choice and placement, editing, mixing and mastering; ORCHESTRAZIONE — professional virtual orchestration, arrangement, real and virtual instruments, sound construction within the production; ANALISI DELLA PRODUZIONE MUSICALE — evolution of the producer's role, the approaches of the most influential producers in history, and the compositional/structural/expressive techniques of the main contemporary popular-music languages, completed with sound design applied to the timbral character of a track; DIRITTO D'AUTORE, ROYALTIES E CONTRATTUALISTICA — copyright, royalties, licence, publishing, production and performance contracts. The bienni are explicitly "costruiti intorno alle inclinazioni artistiche di ciascuno studente", built around each student's own artistic direction, with original productions and third-party commissioned work running through the whole degree.

Also mandatory: download and check the Piano di studi, which lists the competences tested in each individual prova.
auditionSpec: Two-stage: (1) pre-selection on the submitted video links; (2) for those who pass, admission tests held ON SITE in Rome over TWO CONSECUTIVE DAYS, in the June and September sessions. program: Master of Science in Music and Acoustic Engineering (Music Engineering track)
university: Politecnico di Milano

whatYouStudy: Verified from the official study plan. MUSIC ENGINEERING (MMI) track, year 1: Advanced Coding Tools and Methodologies (10 CFU); Computer Music — Representations and Models (5); Multimedia Signal Processing (10); Sound Analysis, Synthesis and Processing (10); Electronics and Electroacoustics for Sound Engineering (10); Fundamentals of Acoustics (compulsory for both tracks); acoustics and vibration analysis. Year 2: Creative Programming and Computing; Music Production Technologies; Music and Acoustic Engineering Capstone; electives from INF/INT/TLC groups covering machine learning, computer graphics and multimedia systems; then a 20-credit thesis. The Acoustic Engineering (MCR) track at Cremona instead covers Musical Acoustics, Room Acoustics and Numerical Modeling and Simulation in Acoustics — note that track drifts towards the acoustics-engineering territory that is out of scope for him.

The single serious obstacle is LANGUAGE: Greek is the primary language of instruction with English only secondary, so he would need to establish before applying how much of his chosen specialisation is actually deliverable in English. Two recommendation letters and an English certificate are also hard requirements he has not yet assembled.

program: Sound Design for Audiovisual Media (M.F.A.)
university: Filmuniversität Babelsberg KONRAD WOLF
durationEcts: 120 LP (ECTS). The official page states 6 semesters; winter-term entry only. Confirm the semester count directly with the programme office.
institutionType: Public film university (Germany's oldest film school; CILECT/GEECT member)
language: German (instruction). Non-German applicants educated outside German-speaking institutions must prove German at DSH-1 level or equivalent; B1 certification is accepted provisionally at application if higher proof is not yet available.
focus: Film/Game Sound; Sound Design; Recording/Engineering; Immersive Audio
whatYouStudy: Four core domains: audio engineering, sound mixing, acoustics and music. Students learn to mix sound for theatrical motion pictures and to run projects as SOUND SUPERVISOR; graduates' competences are stated as equivalent to a Diplom-Tonmeister. Delivered through interdisciplinary collaboration on artistic projects with the university's directing, cinematography and production students, plus collaborations and contacts with the German film industry (Studio Babelsberg is next door).
entryRequirements: 'Proof of a completed Bachelor of Fine Arts (B.F.A.) degree in Sound, Tonmeister*in or a comparable subject-specific degree.' Plus German at DSH-1. An administrative application fee is charged (amount UNVERIFIED).
acceptsNonMusic: No. The requirement is explicitly a B.F.A. 'in Sound, Tonmeister*in or a comparable SUBJECT-SPECIFIC degree', and the entrance exam includes a piano audition and score-harmony analysis. A software-engineering BSc will not clear this bar.
portfolioSpec: Three components, all mandatory: (1) a documentation of works and projects from the last three years revealing the applicant's individual artistic position, MAXIMUM 12 PAGES; (2) video material totalling MAXIMUM 15 MINUTES including AT LEAST THREE FILMS on which the applicant did the sound design (MPG/MPEG/MP4/MOV/WMV, max 3.5 GB); (3) at least one piece of MUSIC that the applicant personally recorded or mixed (WAV/MP3/MP4, max 5 GB).
auditionSpec: Three-part on-site entrance examination. Part 1 MUSIC TEST: hearing/interval identification, score harmony analysis, a PIANO AUDITION, and evaluation of audio examples. Part 2 INTERVIEW: portfolio presentation plus questioning on acoustics and recording technology. Part 3 ARTISTIC/PRACTICAL EXAM: create a soundtrack for a short film using Pro Tools and present an analysis of its tonal dramaturgy.
applicationOpens: 12 April (as published on the official application page)
deadline: 12 April – 18 May 2027 as currently published on the official page, for winter-semester entry. This aligns with an autumn 2027 start — but confirm on the page when the cycle opens, as film-university dates occasionally shift.
tuitionIntl: No tuition fee stated; a semester/administrative fee applies but the amount is UNVERIFIED on the pages read. German public film universities normally charge only a semester contribution.
scholarship: None found on the programme pages. DAAD would be the external route — UNVERIFIED.
fundingLevel: UNVERIFIED (tuition-free public institution, but no named scholarship confirmed)
facilities: Germany's oldest and largest film university, adjacent to Studio Babelsberg; strong industry pipeline. Specific studio and Atmos inventory UNVERIFIED.
fitNotes: Elite, essentially tuition-free, and the Tonmeister-level training is superb — but it is the single hardest gate in this slice for him. It demands a sound/Tonmeister B.F.A., German at DSH-1, three existing films with his sound design, a self-recorded/mixed music piece, AND a piano audition with harmony analysis. Realistically closed unless he first does a sound bachelor. Listed for completeness, not as a target.

program: MA Composition and Theory — Major in Sound Design

Worth attempting with a year of music-theory prep.
portfolioSpec: 3–4 creative works totalling approximately 10 MINUTES MAXIMUM. Formats: scores/texts as PDF, audio as MP3, video as MP4 — all compressed into a SINGLE ZIP file of max 1.95 GB. auditionSpec: On-site aptitude test in three parts: (1) PRACTICAL EXAM — sound-design tasks, 90 minutes preparation then a 20-minute presentation; (2) ORAL EXAM — film/game analysis, 60 minutes preparation then a 10-minute discussion, plus presentation of your submitted works; (3) MUSICAL APTITUDE TEST — theory tasks and improvisation, 30 minutes.

The obstacles are the 30-minute musical aptitude test with improvisation, an on-site two-day aptitude exam in Zurich, and unverified (but certainly high) Swiss living costs.

whatYouStudy: Composition/creation with technology in the Sonic Arts stream. The Sonic Arts Lab is 'the main teaching and research space for students and faculty in the Sonic Arts program' and 'houses a 8 channel sound diffusion system that can be configured for a range of purposes including high order ambisonics, spatial composition, loudspeaker orchestras, or multichannel sound installations', plus a workstation with advanced sound-processing software and a variety of microphones and field-recording equipment. MIAM also runs an Immersive Lab, a professional recording studio, a Percussion Lab, a Sound Gallery, concert/seminar halls and a music library. Concentration areas alongside Sonic Arts include Sound Engineering and Design, Composition, Theory, Musicology, Ethnomusicology, Performance and Music Business & Management. Detailed Sonic Arts module list UNVERIFIED.
portfolioSpec: PRIOR CYCLE (İTÜ MIAM 2022–2023 Entrance Exam Handbook) — confirm the current handbook. Sonic Arts: 'Composition portfolio (Audio + Scores if available). Any other relevant material is also welcome.' Explicitly: 'Optional: Custom made software of projects that have developed as a sample of programming skills including MaxMSP, SuperCollider, Processing etc.' Portfolio is emailed (not uploaded): files under 25 MB attached, larger files as a Google Drive / WeTransfer / Dropbox link, subject line '[MIAM20xx] Your Name & Surname'. A separate MIAM Entrance Exam Contact Form (name, surname, preferred concentration area, phone, e-mail) must accompany it. Note: sending the portfolio is an extra step and does NOT replace official registration at www.sis.itu.edu.tr.
auditionSpec: Yes — on-site. 'ITU MIAM Entrance Exam and the interviews will be held in-person.' Structure (2022 cycle): a written General Music Knowledge and Music Theory exam (12:30–14:30), then a field exam for the chosen concentration area — Sonic Arts is explicitly listed among the masters field exams (15:00–17:00) — then individual interviews spread over the following ~3 days. Requires travel to Istanbul.
entryRequirements: Bachelor's degree; application governed by 'Istanbul Technical University Graduate Level Regulations and Senate Principles'. Two letters of recommendation are required 'to verify their motivation and determination', plus a portfolio relevant to the application area. Online pre-registration via www.sis.itu.edu.tr. ALES/GRE and the exact English-proficiency score threshold follow İTÜ Graduate School rules — exact required scores UNVERIFIED (not stated on the MIAM pages read). IELTS/TOEFL will be needed — he has not yet taken one.
acceptsNonMusic: CHECK — leaning favourable for this concentration. Neither the MIAM admission page nor the entrance-exam handbook read states any requirement for a music bachelor; selection runs on portfolio + exams. The Sonic Arts portfolio explicitly invites 'Custom made software ... including MaxMSP, SuperCollider, Processing' as evidence of programming skills, which directly rewards a software-engineering background. The real obstacle is the compulsory written 'General Music Knowledge and Music Theory' exam, which is not waived for non-music applicants. Formal wording on non-music bachelors: UNVERIFIED — confirm with miam@itu.edu.tr.
deadline: PRIOR CYCLE — confirm new date. 2022 cycle: portfolio submission 24 June; online registration via SIS 27 June; written exams 29 June; interviews 29–30 June and 1 July. For a September 2027 start expect an equivalent late-June 2027 window plus a separate spring-semester round (a 2024–2025 Bahar/spring guide also exists, published late January).
applicationOpens: PRIOR CYCLE — typically announced on the MIAM news page in May (2024–2025 guide published 23 May 2024) for the autumn intake, and late January for the spring intake. 2027 dates not yet published.
scholarship: Türkiye Bursları (YTB) — Arts Scholarship Programme. İTÜ is one of only three universities in that programme (with Ankara Music and Fine Arts University and Ankara Hacı Bayram Veli University), and the music/performing-arts fields listed for it explicitly include music technology at master's level. Open to citizens of all countries except Türkiye; master's applicants need a minimum 75% prior academic average and to be under 30.
fundingLevel: Full (if Türkiye Bursları is awarded); otherwise low-cost public tuition
stipend: Türkiye Bursları master's package: 6,500 TL monthly stipend, full tuition coverage, accommodation, health insurance, a one-year Turkish language course, and round-trip airfare at programme start and completion.
tuitionIntl: UNVERIFIED. İTÜ's own pages confirm international students pay a tuition/contribution fee set annually by the Council of Higher Education and payable in two instalments to Vakıfbank, but the numeric table was not accessible. Third-party sites quote roughly USD 2,000–5,000/year for İTÜ graduate programmes — treat as unconfirmed.
facilities: Recording Studio; Sonic Arts Lab (8-channel diffusion, high-order ambisonics, spatial composition, loudspeaker orchestras, multichannel installations); Immersive Lab; Percussion Lab; Sound Gallery; one large and two medium concert halls; large music library with printed and audiovisual materials. Staff: 2 professors, 9 associate professors, 16 instructors from several countries. Currently ~141 master's and ~73 PhD students. MIAM reports 500+ graduates, many accepted for doctorates at Stanford, Columbia, UC Berkeley and Johns Hopkins. Located on the İTÜ Maçka campus in Beşiktaş, central Istanbul.
fitNotes: Strongest single fit in this slice: fully in English, in a major electronic-music city, with a fully-funded government scholarship route (Türkiye Bursları Arts) that explicitly covers İTÜ music technology at master's level. His coding background is an asset here rather than a liability. Main obstacle: the compulsory written music-theory and general-music-knowledge exam plus an in-person Istanbul entrance exam — he would need roughly a year of deliberate music-theory preparation, and he must sit IELTS/TOEFL.

program: Music (M.A.) — Sound Engineering and Design concentration area (Ses Mühendisliği ve Tasarımı)
university: Istanbul Technical University (İTÜ) — Dr. Erol Üçer Center for Advanced Studies in Music (MIAM)
institutionType: Public technical university; specialist music research centre and graduate school within it
degree: M.A. (Music), thesis track; non-thesis evening variant also available
focus: Recording / Engineering; Music Production; Immersive Audio
durationEcts: 4 semesters normal, 6 maximum; 36 credits required for graduation. ECTS equivalent UNVERIFIED.
whatYouStudy: Studio recording, mixing and mastering practice, sound design, and audio engineering, taught around MIAM's professional recording studio, Immersive Lab and Sonic Arts Lab. Detailed course list UNVERIFIED (the İTÜ Bologna/tyyc pages read did not expose the module tables). Graduates are described by MIAM as sound designers and creative professionals; MIAM's stated mission is to train 'researchers, performance artists, sound designers and creative professionals'.
portfolioSpec: PRIOR CYCLE (2022–2023 handbook) — confirm current version. Sound Engineering and Design, verbatim: '3 mixes of recordings that you made. All mixes must have at least one track that is from an acoustic source (i.e., recorded with a microphone).' Plus '1 Page description of the mixes sent', giving: when the recording was done, where it was done, what equipment was used, what software was used, and credits. 'Photos from recordings as well as other supporting material are welcome.' Delivered by e-mail (<25 MB attached, larger as a cloud link) with the MIAM Entrance Exam Contact Form.
auditionSpec: Yes — on-site in Istanbul. Written General Music Knowledge and Music Theory exams, followed by a Sound Engineering and Design field exam, followed by an individual interview. A secondary report indicates the selection is '3 exams plus an interview', with sound-engineering and music-theory exams weighted heavily, and that applicants present recordings they made using various microphones during the interview — treat that last detail as UNVERIFIED (not from an official page).
entryRequirements: Bachelor's degree; İTÜ Graduate Level Regulations and Senate Principles; two letters of recommendation; portfolio; online pre-registration at www.sis.itu.edu.tr. ALES/GRE and exact English score thresholds UNVERIFIED.
acceptsNonMusic: CHECK — harder than Sonic Arts. No published field restriction was found, but the portfolio requires three of the candidate's own multitrack mixes including a microphone-recorded acoustic source, and the compulsory written music-theory exam is not waived. A CS graduate can satisfy the portfolio only if he has genuine recording/mixing work with acoustic sources. Formal wording on non-music bachelors: UNVERIFIED.
deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. 2022 cycle: portfolio 24 June, SIS registration 27 June, exams 29 June, interviews 29 June – 1 July. Expect a comparable late-June 2027 window.
applicationOpens: PRIOR CYCLE — guide typically posted on the MIAM news page in May for autumn entry (2024–2025 guide: 23 May 2024). 2027 dates unpublished.
scholarship: Türkiye Bursları (YTB) Arts Scholarship Programme — İTÜ is one of the three participating universities; music technology is listed among the eligible master's-level fields. Applications 10 January – 20 February each year.
fundingLevel: Full (if Türkiye Bursları awarded); otherwise low-cost public tuition
stipend: 6,500 TL/month at master's level, full tuition, accommodation, health insurance, one-year Turkish course, return airfare.
tuitionIntl: UNVERIFIED — İTÜ confirms international students pay a state-set fee in two instalments; the fee table itself was not accessible.
facilities: Professional recording studio; Immersive Lab; Sonic Arts Lab with 8-channel diffusion and high-order ambisonics; Sound Gallery; concert halls; music library. 27 academic staff; ~141 master's students. Alumni progress to doctorates at Stanford, Columbia, UC Berkeley, Johns Hopkins.
fitNotes: The most industry-facing English-taught recording/mixing master's in the region, with a genuine full-funding route. But the portfolio is the strictest in this slice for a self-taught electronic producer: three mixes each containing a microphone-recorded acoustic track means he must build a real recording body of work before applying. Sonic Arts at the same institution is the easier door for him.

program: Аудиопродукция и мастеринг (Audio Production and Mastering) — MA, within the 'Музикални медийни технологии и тонрежисура' specialty
university: Sofia University 'St. Kliment Ohridski' — Faculty of Educational Sciences and Arts (ФНОИ)
city: Sofia (also listed by the university's Burgas branch — confirm campus)
institutionType: Public university (largest and oldest in Bulgaria)
focus: Music Production; Recording / Engineering; mastering
durationEcts: 3 semesters, full-time ('редовна'), fee-paying ('платено обучение'), winter-semester intake. ECTS total UNVERIFIED.
whatYouStudy: Compulsory music-theory disciplines, compulsory specialised disciplines, elective and optional disciplines, with specialised preparation in tonrezhisura (sound direction), audio editing, sound engineering and mastering processes. The programme is aimed at people 'with a pronounced interest in contemporary digital sound technologies', with the aim of training highly qualified specialists able to respond to the challenges facing sound designers and sound engineers in the era of contemporary sound technologies.
portfolioSpec: An independently developed AUDIO PROJECT must be presented at the admission interview — the page names as acceptable examples 'композиция, ремикс, рекламен спот, и др.' (a composition, a REMIX, an advertising spot, etc.). No number-of-works, duration or file-format specification is published — confirm with the programme director. This is the single most accessible portfolio requirement found anywhere in this slice for a self-taught electronic producer: a remix is explicitly named.
auditionSpec: Admission interview ('приемен изпит-събеседване') on the presented audio project. No live instrumental audition and no written music-theory exam is published for entry. Whether the interview can be held online for overseas candidates is UNVERIFIED.
entryRequirements: A completed bachelor's degree, with a diploma grade not lower than 'добър' (Good). Diploma or, if not yet issued, an academic transcript stating the average grade and qualification obtained. Ranking is by diploma grade plus the interview.
acceptsNonMusic: YES (apparently) — the published condition is simply 'студенти завършили бакалавърска степен' (students who have completed a bachelor's degree), with no subject-field restriction. This contrasts sharply with the sister programme Audiovisual Design at the same faculty, which explicitly restricts entry to bachelors in Music Education Pedagogy (field 1.3) or Music and Dance Arts (field 8.3). Worth confirming in writing with the director that a foreign engineering BSc is accepted.
deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. FNOI publishes a 'Прием в ОКС Магистър' announcement each year (2025–2026 edition published for that cycle); intake is from the winter semester, so applications typically fall in September. The 2027/28 call is not yet published.
applicationOpens: UNVERIFIED — historically late summer (August–September) for the winter-semester intake.
scholarship: None found specifically attached to this programme. Bulgaria operates state scholarship quotas for foreign nationals via the Ministry of Education and bilateral agreements, but no Tunisia-specific award was verified.
fundingLevel: UNVERIFIED — the programme is explicitly fee-paying ('платено обучение')
tuitionIntl: UNVERIFIED. FNOI publishes a semester fee table (Такси Магистри семестриални 2025–2026) but the PDF could not be parsed; request the figure from the faculty.
facilities: UNVERIFIED for this programme specifically. Programme director: Prof. Dr. Adrian Georgiev (aggeorgiev@uni-sofia.bg, +359 2 970 62 45).
fitNotes: On paper the single most accessible entry route in the whole slice for him: any bachelor accepted, and the entrance 'portfolio' can be a remix he produces himself. The blockers are language (all instruction in Bulgarian — he would need a Bulgarian preparatory year or self-study) and the absence of any verified funding, since the programme is fee-paying by design.

program: Тонрежисура (Sound Engineering / Tonmeister) — master's programme
university: New Bulgarian University (Нов български университет, NBU) — Department of Music
institutionType: Private accredited university
degree: Master's; professional qualification awarded: 'магистър по тонрежисура'
focus: Recording / Engineering; Electronic Music; Music Production; Film & Game Sound
durationEcts: 2 semesters / 63 credits for holders of a music-and-dance-arts bachelor. For graduates of OTHER fields: an individualised curriculum of MINIMUM 3 semesters, the first of which is preparatory. Credit split published as: 4 lecture courses (12 cr), 2 practical courses (6 cr), 5 training courses in semester 1 (15 cr), 6 courses in semester 2 (30 cr).
whatYouStudy: Published scope: тонрежисура (sound direction), звукови технологии (audio technologies), софтуерни решения в музикалното студио (software solutions in the music studio), електронен звук (electronic sound), звуков монтаж (audio editing), аудиодизайн на звук (sound design), синтез на звук (sound synthesis), мастеринг (mastering), звук в киното и телевизията (sound in film and television), and компютърно моделиране на звуковата картина (computer modelling of the sound picture). NBU describes the programme as practice-oriented with exchange opportunities at European institutions. Graduation is by master's thesis defence or state exam.
portfolioSpec: Not a formal portfolio. The specialised music entrance exam requires an essay on the theme 'Защо искам да се обучавам в тази специалност' (Why I want to study in this specialty). Candidates 'may also present compositions or developed audio projects to the commission' — i.e. a portfolio is invited but optional. No number, length or format is prescribed.
auditionSpec: Specialised exam (essay) plus an interview with the admissions commission; exam fee 40 BGN. The general aptitude test (ТОП, a 100-minute online exam, 40 BGN, retakeable with the highest score counting) is REQUIRED for most candidates but foreign citizens and applicants who already hold a higher-education degree are exempt — so he would be exempt on both counts. Whether the essay/interview can be sat remotely is UNVERIFIED.
entryRequirements: A completed bachelor's degree. Foreign citizens and holders of an existing higher-education degree are exempt from the ТОП aptitude test.
acceptsNonMusic: YES — explicitly. The programme documents a formal pathway: applicants with a bachelor in music and dance arts complete the programme in 2 semesters, while 'graduates from other fields follow an individualised curriculum lasting a minimum of 3 semesters, with the first being preparatory'. This is the clearest published accommodation of a non-music bachelor found in this entire slice.
deadline: PRIOR/CURRENT CYCLE - confirm new date. NBU runs three ranking rounds per year; 2026 rounds were: July I — register by 3 July, results 8 July; July II — register by 24 July, results 29 July; August — register by 14 August, results 18 August. Expect an equivalent July–August 2027 sequence for a September 2027 start.
applicationOpens: UNVERIFIED for 2027 — ТОП test sessions in 2026 ran June–August, with registration rolling from spring.
scholarship: None found for this programme. NBU offers internal reductions (25% family, 50% disability, 50% full orphan; 25% off the first semester for NBU's own bachelor graduates) — none of which apply to an external Tunisian applicant.
tuitionIntl: Programme-specific figure UNVERIFIED. NBU's published master's fee bands: two-semester programmes 1,800–2,000 EUR per semester; three-semester programmes 1,600–1,800 EUR per semester. On the 3-semester non-music track that implies roughly 4,800–5,400 EUR total. Fees are guaranteed unchanged for the whole period of uninterrupted study.
facilities: UNVERIFIED — no studio inventory published on the pages read. Department head: Prof. Dr. Milena Shushulova (+359 2 8110 504). Programme director: Dr. Ana Lincheva (alincheva@nbu.bg, 02/8110 505).
fitNotes: The best structural fit for his exact profile in the Balkans: NBU has already designed a route for people arriving from non-music degrees, with a preparatory first semester. Content (electronic sound, synthesis, mastering, studio software) maps directly onto DJ/producer ambitions. Two real blockers: instruction is entirely in Bulgarian, and it is a self-pay private university with no funding route identified.

program: Arta Sunetului de Film (Film Sound Art) — master
university: UNATC 'I.L. Caragiale' — National University of Theatre and Cinematography, Faculty of Film
institutionType: Public film and theatre school (national arts university)
focus: Film & Game Sound; Sound Design; Immersive / multichannel audio
language: Romanian. Film Sound is NOT among UNATC's English-taught masters (those are Art of Game Design, Audiovisual Archives: Preservation and Programming, Interactive Technologies for Performing and Media Arts, and Visual Effects).
durationEcts: 2 years / 4 semesters / 120 credits
whatYouStudy: Year 1: Sound Design; Sound Capture and Editing; Foley Art; Research and Creative Cinematography Workshop; Internship and Practice. Year 2: Advanced Sound Design; Film Sound Production/Post-production; Multichannel Mixing; Research and Creative Cinematography Workshop; Internship and Practice; Dissertation. The department states master's students 'concentrate on aspects related to the process of recording and processing sound, both for film and for games or virtual reality', and students work on real productions — fiction, documentary and animation — collaborating across departments to build professional portfolios. 13 specialised instructors.
portfolioSpec: Dossier must contain: a CV in EuroPass format; and a portfolio of 'lucrări artistice cu design sonor realizat de către candidat' (artistic works with sound design created by the candidate), which may include digital copies of films or relevant sound-design projects. In addition, the candidate must BRING TO THE ORAL EXAM the DAW PROJECT FILE for one portfolio work of their own choosing. No minimum/maximum number of works and no duration requirement is published.
auditionSpec: On-site, single evaluation stage in two parts. Proba 1 (written): 'probă de cultură cinematografică' — a film-culture exam based on a set bibliography, plus technical knowledge of sound design. Proba 2 (oral): presentation and discussion of one self-selected portfolio work, with a live DAW project demonstration. Minimum passing grade 6.0/10.
entryRequirements: Completion of 'o specializare cu 180 credite sau 240 credite'. Foreign applicants must demonstrate Romanian at B1 minimum or complete a preparatory year (exemptions only for those with Romanian-medium credentials or a B1+ certificate from an accredited Romanian institution). Registration exclusively via the 2BitsEDU online platform, with portfolios uploaded electronically to a secure candidate folder. Places: 3 state-funded (bugetate) + 3 tuition-based per the admissions page; the department page states 5 places — confirm the 2027 figure.
acceptsNonMusic: YES. The published eligibility is simply having 'absolvit o specializare cu 180 credite sau 240 credite' — no field of study is specified. UNATC's parallel non-EU English-programme page also lists Computer Science among relevant prior fields for its film-faculty masters, reinforcing that engineering backgrounds are contemplated.
deadline: CURRENT CYCLE (Sept 2026 entry), NOT 2027 — confirm the 2027 dates when published. 2026 cycle: registration 4 August – 9 September 2026; file verification 10–11 September 2026; exam period 15–20 September 2026. For a September 2027 start expect the same August–September 2027 pattern.
applicationOpens: CURRENT CYCLE: 4 August 2026 (a separate May–July pre-registration window applies to the English-taught masters). 2027 window not yet published.
scholarship: Romanian Government scholarships offered through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MAE), open specifically to non-EU citizens — Tunisia qualifies. Covers almost all academic fields except Medicine, Dental Medicine and Pharmacy. Requires an average of at least 7/10 (or 'Good') from the last school graduated.
fundingLevel: Full (if the Romanian Government / MAE scholarship is awarded); plus 3 domestic tuition-free 'buget' places at programme level
stipend: Romanian Government MAE scholarship: no tuition or registration fees, a monthly stipend, university accommodation where space allows, and a FREE preparatory year of Romanian language for non-speakers — which conveniently solves the B1 Romanian entry condition.
tuitionIntl: UNVERIFIED. UNATC publishes 'TAXE DE ȘCOLARIZARE 2026-2027' as a Senate-approved PDF but the figures were not retrievable; contact secretariat@unatc.ro or study@unatc.ro.
facilities: UNVERIFIED in detail. Curriculum implies Foley stage and multichannel mixing facilities; students work on live fiction, documentary and animation productions alongside directing, cinematography and editing departments. 13 specialised teaching staff.
fitNotes: The best fully-funded route in the slice for someone with no music degree: eligibility is purely credit-based, the government scholarship covers everything including a free Romanian language year, and the DAW-project oral exam rewards practical production skill over conservatory training. The catch is direction of travel — this is film/game sound and Foley, not club music production, so it serves the sound-design half of his ambition rather than the DJ half. He also needs a portfolio with sound design applied to picture, which he does not yet have.

program: Muzička produkcija (Music Production) — master academic studies (MAS)
university: Academy of Arts, University of Novi Sad (Akademija umetnosti, Univerzitet u Novom Sadu)
institutionType: Public art academy within a public university

focus: Music Production; Electronic Music; Film/Media music production

Electives (choose 12 ECTS): Драматургија савременог филма; Методе у музичком образовању у дигиталном окружењу; Историја електроакустичке музике (History of Electroacoustic Music); Историја популарне музике (History of Popular Music); Продукција музике за нове медије (Production of Music for New Media); Музика у медијима (Music in Media).
portfolioSpec: UNVERIFIED for the master level — the annual Konkurs PDF listing entrance-exam content, quotas and fees could not be retrieved. The sister programme Snimanje i dizajn zvuka at the same academy is documented at 5 places. Request the current Konkurs text from the academy before applying.
auditionSpec: UNVERIFIED — an entrance aptitude check is standard for Serbian art academies, but the specific content for this programme was not confirmed on a page actually read.
entryRequirements: UNVERIFIED in detail. Serbian master academic studies of 60 ECTS normally require a completed 240-ECTS undergraduate degree. Confirm via the academy's Konkurs.
acceptsNonMusic: UNVERIFIED — no published statement found either way. Given the curriculum's heavy production/media orientation (rather than performance), it is worth asking directly, but assume an artistic or music-related prior degree may be expected.
deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. The academy publishes an annual 'Konkurs za upis na master, specijalističke i doktorske akademske studije'; the most recent retrievable full text was the 2022/23 edition. Serbian master admissions typically run in September–October.
applicationOpens: UNVERIFIED
scholarship: None found. Serbia offers budget-financed places but these overwhelmingly go to domestic candidates.
tuitionIntl: UNVERIFIED for this academy. (For comparison, FDU Belgrade charges non-neighbouring foreigners double the domestic self-financing rate.)
facilities: UNVERIFIED. The academy has run a Sound Recording and Sound Design programme since 2003 within its Department of Audio-visual Media, and also runs a four-year undergraduate Music Production and Sound Design degree, so studio infrastructure exists.
fitNotes: Curriculum-wise this is the closest match in the whole slice to what he actually wants — a one-year master literally called Music Production, with electives in electroacoustic music history, popular music history and music production for new media. The problems are informational and practical: entrance requirements, fees and portfolio spec are all unpublished online, teaching is in Serbian, and no funding route was found. Worth a direct e-mail enquiry rather than dismissal.

program: Ses Teknolojileri / Ses Teknolojisi (Sound Technology) — yüksek lisans (thesis and non-thesis)
university: Bahçeşehir University (BAU) — Graduate School (launched under the Graduate School of Natural and Applied Sciences)
city: Istanbul (classes in the Galata campus studios)
institutionType: Private (foundation) university
degree: Yüksek lisans (master's) — both tezli (thesis) and tezsiz (non-thesis) variants exist
focus: Music Production; Recording / Engineering; Film sound; Electronic Music
durationEcts: Non-thesis variant (verified on BAU's ECTS information package): 90 ECTS over 3 semesters, 10 courses plus a project course. A thesis variant of roughly 2 years also exists — its exact credit load is UNVERIFIED (a third-party listing quotes 120 credits / 2 years).
whatYouStudy: Stated objective: 'Recording, mixing, mastering and production for the music industry, sound technique (acoustic, sound signing, sound information access), sound design for media (sound recording and production for cinema and TV).' portfolioSpec: None published. No portfolio, no audition is specified — confirm with the coordinator whether an interview or work sample is used in practice.
auditionSpec: None published. Selection criteria beyond the diploma are set case-by-case by the Institute Board — UNVERIFIED whether an interview is held.
entryRequirements: A bachelor's degree or equivalent diploma, plus criteria set by the Institute Management Board and Senate. Turkish nationals normally require ALES; the requirement for international applicants is UNVERIFIED. Programme coordinator: Prof. Dr. Yahya Burak Tamer (burak.tamer@bau.edu.tr).
acceptsNonMusic: LIKELY YES. No field restriction is published — the entry condition is simply a bachelor's or equivalent diploma — and the programme is deliberately built to draw electives from engineering and communication faculties, implying a technical intake is expected. No explicit wording on non-music bachelors was found, so confirm.
deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. The programme launch announcement gave an application close of 3 September (year not stated on the page). BAU runs multiple graduate intakes per year. 2027 dates unpublished.
applicationOpens: UNVERIFIED
scholarship: None found. Türkiye Bursları does NOT list BAU among its Arts Scholarship universities (only Ankara Music and Fine Arts University, Ankara Hacı Bayram Veli University and İTÜ), so the YTB arts route does not apply here.
fundingLevel: None found — treat as SELF-PAY FALLBACK
tuitionIntl: UNVERIFIED — BAU publishes a 2026–2027 graduate fee table but it is rendered dynamically and returned no rows; request the Ses Teknolojileri figure from the Graduate School.

The two hard limits are that it is taught in Turkish and that it is a private university with no funding path found, so it belongs on the self-pay fallback list unless he first does a Turkish language year.

program: Diplomski studij Montaža — usmjerenje Oblikovanje zvuka (MA Editing — Sound Design specialization)
university: Academy of Dramatic Art (Akademija dramske umjetnosti, ADU), University of Zagreb
institutionType: Public film/theatre academy within a public university
focus: Film & Game Sound; Sound Design; theatre, radio and performing-arts sound
language: Croatian — 'Prijamni ispiti, kao i nastava na ADU održavaju se na hrvatskom jeziku'
durationEcts: 2 years / 4 semesters / 120 ECTS
whatYouStudy: Though formally a module of the Montaža (Editing) master, it is 'largely conceived as an independent program'. It aims to educate creative and professional practitioners who acquire sound knowledge and skills through artistic, theoretical and professional subjects, for film and television as well as for other performing, broadcast and stage arts. Courses dealing with film sound are tied to practical work, individual and team-based: sound-design students realise film, television, radio and stage works produced by ADU's other departments and collaborate with other University of Zagreb faculties. Teaching staff are working sound recordists, sound editors, music editors, re-recording mixers and sound designers. Graduates work across film, television, theatre, radio, performing arts, multimedia projects and video games.
portfolioSpec: EXACT, from the official 2026/27 entrance-exam document. Stage (A) submission, all eliminatory: (1) životopis (CV); (2) motivacijsko pismo — motivation letter, up to 2 'kartice' of text (~3,600 characters); (3) an audiovisual work for which the candidate conceived the sound picture or participated in creating it; (4) a written analysis of that submitted audiovisual work explaining the sound-picture concept AND listing the origin of the noises, music, sound effects and computer programs used in sound post-production. Positive evaluation of BOTH the audiovisual work and the written analysis is a precondition for reaching stage (B). (An older ADU booklet additionally specified DVD-video format in at least 3 copies and three copies of the analysis — check the current submission format.)
auditionSpec: Yes — on-site, three-part, out of 100 points, with a hard 80/100 pass threshold. (1) klauzurni rad (supervised in-house practical exam) up to 20 points; (2) izlaganje koncepta zvučne slike za zadani predložak — presentation of a sound-picture concept for a given template/brief, up to 30 points; (3) razgovor s povjerenstvom (interview) up to 50 points. The commission assesses knowledge of film history, film-music history and music history, and recognition of musical forms, styles and genres. Recommended reading includes Sonnenschein, 'Sound Design: The Expressive Power of Music, Voice and Sound Effects in Cinema', and Weis & Belton, 'Film Sound'.
entryRequirements: For Montaža the published prerequisite is a 'trogodišnji sveučilišni ili stručni prijediplomski studij, 180 ECTS bodova' — a three-year university OR professional undergraduate degree of 180 ECTS. Croatian-language competence is expected in speech and writing; ADU requires no certificate but 'Povjerenstva Prijamnih ispita imaju pravo eliminirati kandidata ... ako ocjene da kandidat ne poznaje hrvatski jezik u mjeri koja je potrebna za uspješno studiranje'. Non-EU nationals compete in a separate foreign-nationals quota with its own priority list.

The direct-admission ('izravni upis') shortcut is reserved for ADU's own Montaža undergraduates, so an external applicant simply takes the full entrance exam. The genuine filter is the exam's assumed knowledge of film and music history, not the bachelor subject.

facilities: The brand association with Abbey Road Studios is the entire proposition and the teaching is genuinely industry-connected. fitNotes: INCLUDED AS A WARNING, not a recommendation. I checked the London and Amsterdam course listings directly: Abbey Road Institute offers Advanced Diplomas and masterclasses only — there is no master's degree at any campus I could verify, and no awarding body is named. For someone who already holds a BSc, paying private-academy fees for an unaccredited diploma is a poor use of money and yields no qualification that European systems recognise at level 7, no automatic student-visa pathway comparable to a degree, and no progression to doctoral study. The craft teaching may well be excellent — but if the goal includes a recognised master's, this is not it. If he wants the Abbey Road name, the 4-day Song Production Masterclass is a far cheaper way to get it.

language: GERMAN. This is the decisive constraint.

scholarship: UNVERIFIED. German students may access BAföG and KOMPASS-Förderung; neither is normally open to a newly-arriving non-EU student.
entryRequirements: Not published on the overview page — UNVERIFIED. A German MA at a state art university will normally require a relevant bachelor plus a portfolio (Mappe) and German at C1. SAE's general validation note reads: "The degree programmes starting from January 2022 are developed, delivered and assessed by SAE Institute, and awarded by and quality assured by the University of Hertfordshire" — but this particular programme is accredited by Folkwang, not Hertfordshire, so its rules differ.
acceptsNonMusic: UNVERIFIED — not addressed on the page read. The project areas listed are broad ("Musik, Film, Video-, Installations- und Medienkunst, Sound-Art, bildende Kunst, Fotografie, Game-Art"), which suggests portfolio-led rather than subject-led admission.
portfolioSpec: UNVERIFIED — no portfolio specification is published on the SAE overview page. Expect a Mappe requirement given the Folkwang involvement. Request the Studien- und Prüfungsordnung directly.
auditionSpec: UNVERIFIED — none published. German art universities typically run an Eignungsprüfung (aptitude test), which may be on-site.
applicationOpens: UNVERIFIED
deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. Not published on the pages read. German art-university intakes typically close between January and April for a September/October start, so for autumn 2027 expect a deadline in the first half of 2027.
facilities: SAE operates ten German campuses (Berlin, Bochum, Frankfurt, Hamburg, Hannover, Köln, Leipzig, München, Nürnberg, Stuttgart) with studios and workspaces; this master's is delivered at Bochum. Folkwang is one of Germany's leading art universities. Specific studio inventory UNVERIFIED.
whatYouStudy: A supervised, self-directed master-level project across "Musik, Film, Video-, Installations- und Medienkunst, Sound-Art, bildende Kunst, Fotografie, Game-Art" — i.e. sound art and music are legitimate project areas, but this is an interdisciplinary media-art master's rather than a music-production course.
fitNotes: Included because it is the only Folkwang-accredited German state-university MA reachable through a private audio academy, which would give him a fully EU-recognised degree. But it is taught in GERMAN, which he does not speak — that alone rules it out for September 2027 unless he starts German now and reaches C1 in about eighteen months. Note also that SAE Germany's other master's ("Masterstudiengang Professional Practice", MA/MSc, 24 months, University of Hertfordshire, online) is likewise delivered in German. If German is not on the table, use the English-language SAE UK/online routes or Catalyst Berlin instead.
